sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the xenon-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local xenon ion number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the number of included xenon ions, and $V$ is a local plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the xenon-ion population immediately adjacent to one divertor target and is summed over all positive xenon ionization states, from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon. Neutral xenon atoms are excluded; this is a local sheath-entrance density, not a volume-averaged density or a density at a general plasma location.

Compared with [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which denotes xenon ion density at a general plasma point, this quantity is specialized to the divertor-target sheath entrance. Its charge-state-summed species convention parallels [oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target), with xenon replacing oxygen.

sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the beryllium-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining density is the zeroth velocity-space moment, summed over all beryllium ionization states:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}}\int f_{\mathrm{Be},z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ identifies a beryllium ionization state, $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the set of included beryllium ionization states, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{\mathrm{Be},z}$ is the velocity distribution function for state $z$, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity applies locally at the plasma boundary and is additive over all included ionic charge states. It includes beryllium ions and excludes neutral beryllium atoms; it is not a flux-surface average.

This is the beryllium-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose particle population is unspecified. It differs from [flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary) because that quantity averages the beryllium-ion density over the boundary surface, and from [beryllium_density_at_limiter](name:beryllium_density_at_limiter), which uses a limiter-adjacent locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Number density of boron at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over neutral atoms and all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of boron at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for elemental boron evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local elemental-boron number density at a boundary point is the zeroth velocity moment summed over neutral boron and all ionic charge states:

$$
n_{\mathrm B}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{z=0}^{5} \int f_{\mathrm B,z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm B}$ is the elemental-boron number density, $\mathrm B$ denotes boron, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $z$ is the boron charge-state index with $z=0$ denoting neutral boron and $z=1$ through $5$ denoting the ionic states, $f_{\mathrm B,z}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to elemental boron and includes neutral atoms together with all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+. It is a local value at the plasma boundary, with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume, and excludes densities of other elements and electrons. Unlike [ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), it is not restricted to charged ions.

It is the boron-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related [flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary) applies the same neutral-plus-ionic boron aggregation but averages the density over the last closed magnetic flux surface rather than giving the local boundary value.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Number density of carbon impurity ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of carbon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the carbon-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment, with explicit aggregation over carbon ionization states, is

$$
n_C(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{q=1}^{6}\int f_{C^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_C$ is the carbon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the integer carbon charge-state index, $f_{C^{q+}}$ is the velocity distribution function of carbon ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies locally to carbon ions in charge states C+ through C6+ and is summed over those ionization states. Neutral carbon is excluded, and the value is not averaged over the boundary flux surface.

It specializes the population-unspecified [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to carbon ions. It is distinct from [flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary), which applies the same carbon-ion aggregation after averaging over the boundary surface, and from [carbon_density](name:carbon_density), whose elemental scope includes neutral carbon as well as ionic charge states.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all ionic charge states, and excluding neutral deuterium.
NAMES.long:
Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the deuterium-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_D(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z>0}\int f_{D^{z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ is a positive ionic charge state, $D^{z+}$ denotes deuterium in charge state $z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{D^{z+}}$ is the velocity distribution function for that charge state, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to deuterium ions, is evaluated locally at the plasma boundary, and is additive over all included positive deuterium charge states. Neutral deuterium atoms and molecules are excluded. It is therefore distinct from the broader [ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), which does not select deuterium, and from [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which applies a flux-surface average rather than a local boundary evaluation.

This species-specific quantity is a specialization of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose particle population and charge-state aggregation are unspecified. The local deuterium value provides the pointwise boundary quantity from which the corresponding flux-surface-averaged deuterium density is formed.

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for that effective species evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local effective deuterium-tritium number density is the zeroth velocity moment of its distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{DT}$ is the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-pseudo-species number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity of the effective pseudo-species, $f_{DT}$ is its phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies to the deuterium-tritium fuel mixture represented as one effective pseudo-species, rather than to separate deuterium and tritium populations. It is a local boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume, and no additional charge-state aggregation is implied by the effective-species representation.

It is the deuterium-tritium-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). Unlike [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), it denotes the local value at the plasma boundary rather than an average over that last closed magnetic flux surface.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the electron population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local electron number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the electron distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_e(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $f_e$ is the electron phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to electrons and is not an ion or neutral-particle density. It is a local boundary value, with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume; because electrons are not resolved here into atomic ionization states, no charge-state aggregation is applied.

It is the electron-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related [flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) instead represents the average of electron density over the same last closed magnetic flux surface, rather than the local value.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron number density averaged over the entire last closed magnetic flux surface, giving the separatrix value across the confined-plasma and scrape-off-layer interface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged electron number density on the separatrix, the last closed magnetic flux surface forming the confined-plasma boundary. It represents the electron population at the complete core–scrape-off-layer interface after averaging over the boundary surface.

For a magnetic-flux surface labeled by $\psi$, the separatrix value is defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm sep} =
\frac{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\rm sep}} n_e\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\rm sep}}\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

where $\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm sep}$ is the flux-surface-averaged electron number density at the separatrix, $n_e$ is the local electron number density, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix surface, $dS$ is its differential surface element, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux surface label, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of that label.

The average covers the entire last closed flux surface at the core–scrape-off-layer boundary. It is an electron-specific quantity, with no ion or neutral population included and no ionization-state summation. It is distinct from the local, pointwise boundary value [electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which is not flux-surface averaged.

The analogous [flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) applies the same separatrix averaging convention to the ion population rather than the electron population.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the helium-3 ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface, or separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local charge-state-summed helium-3 number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the helium-3 ion distribution functions at a boundary point:

$$
n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{2} \int f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $q$ is the helium-3 ionic charge state, $f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to helium-3 ions, whose nuclei contain three nucleons, and includes all ionized charge states from singly charged through fully stripped helium-3. It excludes neutral helium-3, other helium isotopes, and other plasma species. The value is local at the boundary and is not averaged over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the helium-3-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related [flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary) represents the average of this local helium-3 ion density over the same last closed magnetic flux surface rather than its value at a boundary point.

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the helium-4 ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the charge-state-summed helium-4 ion population at that locus.

The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_q\int f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the ionic charge-state index, $f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}$ is the velocity distribution function of helium-4 ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This quantity applies only to helium-4 ions, is evaluated locally at the boundary, includes all helium-4 ionic charge states, and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms.

As a species-specific instance of [particle number density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), it fixes the otherwise unspecified population to helium-4 ions. It differs from [flux-surface-averaged helium-4 density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary), which averages the same charge-state-summed population over the boundary surface, and from [helium-3 density at the plasma boundary](name:helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary), which selects a different helium isotope.

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all hydrogen ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the hydrogen-ion population on the last closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_H(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_H(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_H$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_H$ is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is evaluated locally at the plasma boundary and is summed over the included hydrogen ion charge states. It excludes neutral hydrogen and is distinct from electron density and from the total ion population represented by [ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The corresponding surface-averaged quantity, [flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), applies the same hydrogen-ion population to an average over the boundary surface rather than a local evaluation. The subject-unspecified parent [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) defines the common boundary-density concept, while this quantity fixes the population as hydrogen ions.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Number density of iron impurity ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer, summed over all ion charge states from Fe+ through fully stripped Fe26+.
NAMES.long:
Iron density at the plasma boundary is the number of iron impurity ions per unit volume — summed over all ion charge states from singly ionized Fe$^+$ through fully stripped Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$) — evaluated at the separatrix, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It represents the charge-state-summed iron impurity concentration on that boundary.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron ion number density at the plasma boundary, $z$ is the positive ion charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of iron ions in charge state $z+$ at the same boundary; these number-density variables have the unit specified for this standard name.

The sum is over ion charge states only, so neutral iron Fe$^0$ is excluded. As a scalar number density, the quantity is non-negative, with zero denoting absence of iron ions at the plasma boundary. It is distinct from [flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which denotes a flux-surface-averaged boundary value rather than the local boundary density.

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the lithium-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{3}\int f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the lithium ionization-state index, $f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}$ is the velocity distribution function for lithium ions in charge state $Z+$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is local at the plasma boundary and is not averaged over the boundary flux surface. It includes lithium ions from Li+ through Li3+, summed over these charge states, and excludes neutral lithium. It is the lithium-specific specialization of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

The corresponding flux-surface-averaged quantity, [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary), applies a flux-surface average to the same charge-state-summed lithium-ion density. The boundary locus also distinguishes this quantity from [lithium density at the limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which is evaluated at a limiter rather than at the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the neon-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The population is summed over all ionization stages from singly ionized neon, Ne$^+$, through fully stripped neon, Ne$^{10+}$.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b)=\int f_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $f_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the velocity distribution function aggregated over the included neon ion charge states, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This quantity is evaluated locally at that boundary and is not averaged over the flux surface. It includes neon ions across all charge states from Ne$^+$ through Ne$^{10+}$ and excludes neutral neon and other particle species.

This quantity is the neon-specific specialization of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). It is distinct from [flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary), which applies the same charge-state aggregation to a flux-surface average rather than a local boundary value.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the nitrogen ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local nitrogen ion number density at a boundary point is the zeroth velocity moment summed over ionic charge states:

$$
n_N(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{7} \int f_{N^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_N$ is the nitrogen ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $q$ is the positive integer ionic charge state, $N^{q+}$ is a nitrogen ion with charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $f_{N^{q+}}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that charge state, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to nitrogen ions and is summed over charge states from singly ionized nitrogen through fully stripped nitrogen. It excludes neutral nitrogen and electron density, and it is a local boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the nitrogen-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related [flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) instead averages the same charge-state-summed nitrogen ion density over the last closed magnetic flux surface.

NAMES.name: total_power_at_separatrix
NAMES.short: Net energy power leaving the confined plasma through the last closed magnetic flux surface and entering the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Separatrix power is the net global energy loss from the confined plasma into the scrape-off layer across the last closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the aggregate power crossing the entire separatrix rather than a local surface value.

The defining boundary integral is

$$
P_{\rm sep} = \oint_{S_{\rm sep}} \mathbf{S}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix power, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the last closed magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{S}_E$ is the net plasma-energy flux density, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the confined plasma toward the scrape-off layer, and $dA$ is an element of separatrix area.

This is a total, net quantity integrated over the complete separatrix. It applies to the confined plasma as a whole, with no selection of species, reaction channel, or individual transport mechanism; outward energy transfer is the plasma loss represented by the quantity. It is not a pointwise energy-flux density or a power associated with a single surface location.

The boundary total is distinct from [radiated power over the core region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region), which describes electromagnetic power emitted within the core and is not necessarily equal to power crossing the separatrix. It is also distinct from [power due to conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), which describes conduction-mediated power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces downstream of the separatrix.

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the tritium-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local tritium-ion number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the tritium-ion distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is tritium-ion velocity, $f_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to ionized tritium and excludes neutral tritium, deuterium, protium, electrons, impurity ions, and total ion density. It is a local boundary value, with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume; for tritium, the relevant positive ion population is singly ionized tritium, so no aggregation over multiple positive ionization stages is applied.

It is the tritium-specific instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related [flux-surface-averaged tritium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary) instead represents the average of tritium-ion density over the same last closed magnetic flux surface, while [hydrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [deuterium density at the plasma boundary](name:deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) refer to different hydrogen-isotope ion populations.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary is the amount of the xenon ion population per physical volume at the last closed magnetic flux surface. It is the local boundary value, not a flux-surface average.

The local charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{54}\int f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the xenon ion charge-state number, $f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}$ is the velocity distribution function for charge state $Z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The aggregation is additive over all xenon ion charge states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral xenon atoms. The value is local at the boundary rather than averaged over that surface.

This entry specializes the population-unspecified [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to xenon ions. The corresponding [flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary) applies the same xenon charge-state aggregation after averaging over the plasma-boundary flux surface, so it is distinct from this local quantity.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal
NAMES.short: Dimensionless radial magnetic-surface label locating the H-mode edge transport-barrier pedestal between the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the dimensionless radial magnetic-surface coordinate assigned to the pedestal position of an H-mode edge transport barrier. It identifies the flux surface associated with that position, rather than a density, pressure, or temperature value evaluated there.

The normalized poloidal-flux coordinate is defined from the poloidal magnetic flux by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{p}} = \left(\frac{\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the normalized poloidal-flux coordinate, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its value on the magnetic axis, and $\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}}$ is its value on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The reported value is this coordinate evaluated at the pedestal position.

This quantity applies specifically to the H-mode edge transport-barrier pedestal locus. It has no species, population, or field-component dependence and involves no averaging or summation over plasma quantities. It retains the generic pedestal-position meaning and is not a pedestal-top profile value or a maximum-gradient location.

It is a locus-specific instance of the parent [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate), applying that coordinate's outward magnetic-surface labeling to the pedestal position rather than to an arbitrary nested surface. For a pedestal within nested closed surfaces, its value lies between zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: thermal_plasma_pressure
NAMES.short: Thermal plasma pressure is the equilibrium isotropic kinetic pressure of thermal electrons and ions, summed over represented ion species and excluding fast-particle contributions.
NAMES.long:
Thermal plasma pressure is the isotropic kinetic pressure of thermal electron and ion populations in a fluid or magnetohydrodynamic description. It represents equilibrium mechanical stress from these populations and is not a perturbation amplitude.

For the included thermal populations, the pressure is defined by

$$
p_{\rm th} = p_{e,\rm th} + \sum_{s \in \mathcal{I}} p_{s,\rm th}
$$

where $p_{\rm th}$ is the thermal plasma pressure, $p_{e,\rm th}$ is the thermal electron pressure, $p_{s,\rm th}$ is the thermal pressure of ion species $s$, and $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of represented ion species.

The quantity applies to the thermal electron population and all represented thermal ion species, with ion contributions aggregated over the included species and charge states. It excludes fast-particle and other nonthermal contributions, neutral-particle pressure, magnetic pressure, dynamic ram pressure, anisotropic pressure components, and first-order pressure perturbations.

Thermal plasma pressure is the thermal specialization of [plasma pressure](name:plasma_pressure), obtained by restricting the parent quantity to thermal electrons and ions. [Thermal ion pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure) supplies the ion contribution in the defining sum, while the electron contribution is included separately.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Non-negative radius-like toroidal-flux label identifying the magnetic flux surface at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the non-negative, radius-like toroidal-flux label of the magnetic flux surface at the H-mode [pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It locates that surface on the physical toroidal-flux scale rather than specifying a geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from enclosed toroidal magnetic flux by:

$$
\rho_{\rm tor} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\rm tor}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\rm tor}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\rm tor}$ is the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux, $B_0$ is the positive reference vacuum toroidal-field magnitude that sets the coordinate scale, and $\pi$ is the circular constant.

The value applies to the single nested magnetic flux surface passing through the pedestal top. It is a local flux-surface label, not a flux-surface or volume average, and it has no particle-population or charge-state aggregation.

This is the pedestal-top specialization of the parent [toroidal flux coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate), obtained by evaluating that coordinate on the pedestal-top surface. Unlike the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the pedestal top](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top), it retains the radius-like physical scale of the toroidal flux coordinate.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_neutral_temperature
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic temperature, expressed as energy per particle, of a neutral population throughout the plasma volume inside the last closed magnetic flux surface during plasma initiation.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic temperature of a neutral population during plasma initiation, representing random translational energy after removal of mean flow. It excludes energy stored in internal excitation or other internal quantum states.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{n} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} T_n(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{T}_{n}$ is the volume-averaged neutral temperature, $T_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local translational kinetic temperature of the neutral population at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies to the represented neutral population throughout the volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface during plasma initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial volume average of the local temperature, not a local value or a density-weighted particle average. It does not select only the cold or energetic neutral component and is not restricted to a particular internal quantum state.

This quantity is obtained by applying the volume-averaging transformation to [neutral temperature](name:neutral_temperature), with the local population and state aggregation inherited from that quantity. [Cold neutral temperature](name:cold_neutral_temperature) and [hot neutral temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature) are population-restricted alternatives, while [neutral internal state temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature) resolves a specified internal state rather than the generic neutral population.

NAMES.name: frequency_of_wave_diagnostic_channel
NAMES.short: Temporal frequency associated with a wave-diagnostic channel, defining the oscillation or probing frequency used to establish its plasma interaction.
NAMES.long:
The wave-diagnostic-channel frequency is the temporal rate of oscillation of the electromagnetic wave associated with a channel. It specifies the frequency at which the channel interacts with or samples the plasma.

The relation between temporal frequency $f$ and angular frequency $\omega$ is

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is the temporal frequency, $\omega$ is the angular frequency of the wave, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

This quantity applies to one wave-diagnostic channel and is not a sum or average over channels, frequency values, or wave power. For a frequency-swept probing channel, each selected frequency defines the probing state used to determine the corresponding plasma response or cutoff location; for a resonance channel, it identifies the wave frequency associated with the probed resonance.

The channel-owned quantity is distinct from the broader [wave frequency](name:wave_frequency) concept and from the beam-owned [frequency of an electron-cyclotron beam](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam). It describes frequency, not the duration of a sweep or the electromagnetic energy-transfer rate represented by [wave power](name:wave_power).

NAMES.name: line_integrated_electron_number_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Free-electron column density accumulated along a complete electromagnetic propagation path, including both forward and return segments when present.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the column density of free electrons encountered along a specified electromagnetic propagation path. It represents the total free-electron content accumulated along the path, rather than the local electron population at a point.

For the complete propagation path, the line-integrated electron density is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = \int_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}} n_e(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-integrated electron density, $n_e(\ell)$ is the local free-electron number density at path position $\ell$, $\ell$ is arclength along the path, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}$ is the complete propagation path.

The integral applies to the free-electron population along the full line of sight and aggregates the local number density over arclength. For a reflected propagation channel, the path includes both forward and return segments, with no factor-of-two correction. The quantity excludes neutral or bound electrons and is distinct from the local [electron density](name:electron_density) and from a path average.

For a path with total arclength $L$, this quantity relates to the [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) through $N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = L\bar{n}_e$, where $L$ is the total path arclength and $\bar{n}_e$ is the path-averaged free-electron number density.

NAMES.name: polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam
NAMES.short: Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma. It describes the beam's post-propagation transverse polarization state, not the incident state or the ellipse orientation.
NAMES.long:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma is the ellipticity of that beam. It characterizes the relative electric-field semiamplitudes of the post-propagation transverse polarization ellipse.

The ellipticity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon = \frac{b}{a}
$$

where $\varepsilon$ is the polarization ellipticity, $a$ is the major-axis semiamplitude of the electric-field polarization ellipse, and $b$ is the signed minor-axis semiamplitude of that ellipse. The magnitude satisfies $|\varepsilon| \leq 1$.

This quantity applies to the polarimeter beam after it has traversed the magnetized plasma and is therefore distinct from the [initial polarization ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam). It is a polarization-shape parameter and excludes the orientation of the ellipse; rotation of that orientation is represented by the [Faraday angle](name:faraday_angle). The quantity refers to a single beam polarization state, with no aggregation over distinct beam paths.

Magnetized-plasma birefringence can transform the [initial polarization ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam) into this post-propagation ellipticity by changing the polarization ellipse during propagation; that change is distinct from Faraday rotation of the ellipse orientation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electric-field vector rotates in a right-handed sense about the beam-propagation direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Ellipticity
sources.parent_definition: Set of channels (lines-of-sight)

NAMES.name: initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam
NAMES.short: Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the electric-field polarization ellipse of a polarimeter probing beam in its incident state, before plasma entry. It gives only the ellipticity component of the initial polarization vector, not the ellipse orientation.
NAMES.long:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the electric-field polarization ellipse of a polarimeter probing beam in its incident state, before plasma entry, is the initial polarization ellipticity of that beam. It is the ellipticity component of the beam's initial polarization vector and specifies the shape and handedness of the incident polarization ellipse, not its orientation.

For an incident electric-field polarization ellipse with major semiaxis amplitude $a_0$ and minor semiaxis amplitude $b_0$, the initial ellipticity $\epsilon_0$ is defined by:

$$
\epsilon_0 = \sigma_0 \frac{b_0}{a_0}
$$

where $\epsilon_0$ is the initial polarization ellipticity, $a_0$ is the major semiaxis amplitude, $b_0$ is the minor semiaxis amplitude with $0 \le b_0 \le a_0$, and $\sigma_0$ is the handedness sign of the incident polarization state.

This quantity applies to a single polarimeter probing beam along a specified line of sight in its pre-plasma state. It is not averaged or summed over multiple lines of sight, and it does not describe the full polarization vector, beam intensity, wavelength, path geometry, path-integrated ellipticity, or any post-plasma polarization state.

It provides the reference value for Cotton-Mouton ellipticity changes induced during traversal of magnetized plasma. It is the incident-state counterpart of [polarization ellipticity of a polarimeter beam](name:polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam), which denotes the polarization ellipticity after plasma traversal; it is distinct from the [Faraday angle](name:faraday_angle), which describes rotation of the polarization-ellipse orientation rather than the semiaxis ratio.
NAMES.sign: Positive when, in the right-handed beam-local basis $(\hat{e}_1, \hat{e}_2, \hat{k})$ with $\hat{k}$ along beam propagation, $\hat{e}_1$ along the major semiaxis, and $\hat{e}_2 = \hat{k} \times \hat{e}_1$, the electric-field vector rotates from $+\hat{e}_1$ toward $+\hat{e}_2$ as time increases.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_measurement_position
NAMES.short: Signed equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function evaluated at a diagnostic measurement location, identifying the nested magnetic surface intersecting that location.
NAMES.long:
The signed poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ is the equilibrium flux function evaluated at a physical measurement position. It labels the nested magnetic surface passing through that position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the poloidal magnetic-flux function is defined by

$$
\psi(R,Z) = \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\psi(R,Z)$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at cylindrical coordinates $(R,Z)$, $B_Z(R',Z)$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, $R$ and $R'$ are major-radius coordinates, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\pi$ is the circle constant. The toroidal angle $\phi$ completes the right-handed cylindrical frame; axisymmetry makes $\psi$ independent of $\phi$.

This quantity applies to the equilibrium magnetic field at one physical measurement position and has no species or population restriction. It is a point evaluation, not a sum, average, or integral over multiple measurement positions. It is not a normalized flux coordinate and does not represent a perturbation or fluctuation of the equilibrium flux.

The same flux-function definition is used for [poloidal magnetic flux at a beam-tracing point](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_beam_tracing_point), but that quantity differs in evaluation locus. A normalized surface label at the same type of location is [normalized poloidal flux coordinate at a measurement position](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position), which is derived by applying axis and boundary references to the signed flux value.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net vertical magnetic flux through the defining horizontal disk is directed in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radiative_temperature_at_ece_channel
NAMES.short: Equivalent blackbody temperature of electron cyclotron emission intensity detected by a frequency-selective ECE channel, representing the radiation brightness temperature.
NAMES.long:
Radiative temperature at an ECE channel is the equivalent blackbody temperature associated with the detected electron cyclotron emission intensity at that channel's selected frequency. It is a brightness-temperature representation of the radiation, not the kinetic temperature of the electron population.

For specific intensity represented by a blackbody spectrum, the radiation temperature $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is defined by

$$
I_\nu = \frac{2h\nu^3}{c^2}\left[\exp\left(\frac{h\nu}{T_{\mathrm{rad}}}\right)-1\right]^{-1}
$$

where $I_\nu$ is the detected specific intensity at frequency $\nu$, $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the energy-equivalent blackbody temperature.

The quantity applies to one ECE channel and its selected frequency; it is not summed or averaged over channels. It excludes the separate kinetic electron temperature and polarization-resolved radiation quantities. When the emitting plasma is optically thick, $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ approaches the local electron temperature. The [radiative temperature at the magnetic axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) uses the same brightness-temperature definition at a different evaluation locus.

NAMES.name: spectral_calibration_factor_at_line_of_sight
NAMES.short: Wavelength-specific interferometric conversion coefficient that converts a signed phase change along a line of sight into electron column density.
NAMES.long:
The spectral calibration factor is the wavelength-specific proportionality that maps an interferometric phase change along one line of sight to the electron column density on that optical path.

The conversion is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = K_{\mathrm{spec}}\,\Delta\varphi
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density), $K_{\mathrm{spec}}$ is this spectral calibration factor, and $\Delta\varphi$ is the signed interferometric phase change.

The factor applies to the complete electron-density integral along the associated line of sight and to its corresponding probing wavelength. It represents the electron contribution only and is not a local density, a line-averaged density, or an optical phase itself.

Applying this factor produces the line-integrated electron number density; dividing that result by the optical chord length gives [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density). The associated wavelength is the spectral parameter of the probing electromagnetic wave, related to [wavelength of wave beam](name:wavelength_of_wave_beam).

NAMES.name: variation_of_length_of_interferometer_beam
NAMES.short: Signed change in the effective optical path length accumulated along an interferometer beam, caused by plasma relative to the corresponding no-plasma reference path.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed plasma-induced change in effective optical path length accumulated along one interferometer-beam line of sight. It captures the integrated refractive effect of the plasma along that path rather than a local geometric displacement.

The defining difference is

$$
\Delta L = L_{\mathrm{plasma}} - L_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\Delta L$ is the plasma-induced optical path-length variation, $L_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the effective optical path length with the plasma contribution present, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the corresponding effective optical path length for the same beam path with the plasma contribution removed.

The quantity applies to all plasma encountered along the complete propagation path of a single interferometer beam, with distributed contributions aggregated into one path-length difference. It has no local spatial, species-resolved, or charge-state-resolved meaning. It excludes the unvaried reference path length and is not the total [effective optical path length](name:length_of_interferometer_beam) of the beam.

This variation is the optical-path quantity associated with the interferometric phase shift and is used to relate the propagation path to the [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density). It remains a path-length difference and must not be identified with the electron column density itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the plasma increases the effective optical path length relative to the corresponding no-plasma reference path.

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short: Fringe-jump-corrected phase angle of a probing electromagnetic signal at a selected wavelength, referenced to the channel’s defined launch phase.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the continuous phase angle of a probing electromagnetic signal at one selected wavelength, with integer-cycle discontinuities caused by fringe jumps removed. It represents the phase accumulated along the signal’s propagation chord relative to the channel’s defined launch-phase reference.

The corrected phase is related to the measured wrapped phase by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{corr}} = \phi_{\mathrm{meas}} + 2\pi N_{\mathrm{fj}}
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the fringe-jump-corrected phase, $\phi_{\mathrm{meas}}$ is the measured wrapped phase, and $N_{\mathrm{fj}}$ is the signed integer number of full-cycle fringe-jump corrections. The factor $2\pi$ represents one complete phase revolution.

The quantity applies to a single probing wavelength and represents the phase accumulated over the complete propagation chord, rather than a local phase at one point. It is referenced to the channel’s defined launch phase; it is not an absolute electromagnetic phase and does not include an uncorrected fringe discontinuity.

The corrected phase is the phase observable used to obtain the [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density) through the wavelength-dependent plasma refractive index. It is distinct from the general [reference phase](name:reference_phase), which establishes a phase origin without specifying fringe-jump correction or a propagation chord.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged along a complete plasma propagation chord, equal to the path integral divided by chord length.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged along a complete propagation chord is the path-normalized continuum count density of the unqualified free-electron population along that chord.

For local [electron density](name:electron_density) $n_e(l)$, the defining relation is:

$$
\bar{n}_e = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_e(l)\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_e$ is the line-averaged electron density, $n_e(l)$ is the local free-electron density at path coordinate $l$, $l$ is distance along the complete propagation chord, and $L$ is the full chord length.

This quantity applies to the complete unqualified free-electron population along the chord, aggregating all contributing free-electron populations rather than selecting thermal or fast electrons. It is a path average over the chord and is not a pointwise [electron density](name:electron_density) or a line-integrated column density.

The numerator in the defining relation is the [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density); dividing it by the chord length produces this path-normalized quantity. The same line-averaging construction applies to species-specific quantities such as [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while this quantity remains specific to free electrons.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position
NAMES.short: Dimensionless radial label that maps a physical measurement position to a nested magnetic surface using the square root of normalized poloidal magnetic flux.
NAMES.long:
The normalized poloidal flux coordinate at a measurement position assigns the physical point to a nested closed magnetic surface through its radial position between the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface. It is the pointwise value of the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) at that measurement location.

The defining normalization is

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}})=\sqrt{\frac{\psi(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}})-\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}-\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$ is the normalized poloidal flux coordinate, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}}$ is the physical measurement position, $\psi(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}})$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at that position, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis, and $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at the last closed flux surface.

This quantity applies to one physical measurement position and has no population or region aggregation: it is evaluated pointwise rather than averaged along a path or over a region. It is a normalized surface label, not a poloidal magnetic-flux value or a toroidal-flux coordinate.

The transformation preserves the parent coordinate's normalization: it is zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed flux surface, with intermediate values identifying nested surfaces between those boundaries.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_beam_tracing_point
NAMES.short: Dimensionless magnetic-surface label obtained from normalized enclosed toroidal flux, evaluated at each beam-tracing point to map the propagation path onto nested plasma surfaces.
NAMES.long:
This quantity assigns the magnetic surface intersected by each beam-tracing point a dimensionless, radial-like toroidal-flux label. It describes the location of the propagation point in nested equilibrium flux surfaces, not a physical distance or a local vector component.

The normalized toroidal flux coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux of the magnetic surface through the beam-tracing point, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its value at the equilibrium boundary.

The quantity is evaluated pointwise at each beam-tracing position for which the nested equilibrium flux surfaces define the coordinate. It applies to the magnetic surface associated with each propagation point and is not aggregated over the beam path, nor does it represent a particle-population property.

This is the beam-tracing-point evaluation of the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). It differs from [normalized toroidal flux coordinate at a measurement position](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position), which assigns the same magnetic-surface coordinate to a specified physical measurement location rather than to a beam-tracing point.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_ece_channel_emission_position
NAMES.short: Dimensionless magnetic-surface label assigned to an electron-cyclotron emission location, locating that emission on nested toroidal-flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The normalized toroidal-flux coordinate at an electron-cyclotron-emission channel's emission position is the magnetic-surface label assigned to the location from which the channel's emission originates.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux of the magnetic surface passing through the emission position, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is that flux at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is that flux at the equilibrium boundary.

This quantity is a point evaluation for one electron-cyclotron-emission channel position, applying to the magnetic surface intersecting that position. It has no sum, average, or integration over channels, line-of-sight points, or emission locations, and it is not a cylindrical radial distance.

It is the emission-position specialization of the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate): within the normalized interval, it is zero at the magnetic axis and reaches one at the equilibrium boundary. Its locus differs from the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate at measurement position](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position), which is evaluated at a measurement position rather than an electron-cyclotron emission position.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position
NAMES.short: Dimensionless toroidal magnetic-surface label assigned to a physical measurement position, locating that position relative to the magnetic axis and equilibrium boundary.
NAMES.long:
The normalized toroidal flux coordinate at a measurement position identifies the nested magnetic surface intersecting that physical location. It is a geometric flux label, independent of the measured plasma quantity.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the magnetic surface through the measurement position, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its value at the equilibrium boundary.

This quantity is evaluated at one physical measurement position and is not a population-dependent value, spatial average, cylindrical radial distance, or local vector component. It maps that position to a magnetic-surface label rather than identifying the measured signal itself.

It is the measurement-position evaluation of the parent [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike [normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position), it is based on toroidal rather than poloidal magnetic flux.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_measurement_position
NAMES.short: Dimensionless magnetic-surface label assigning the Doppler reflectometer measurement location to a normalized toroidal-flux surface between the magnetic axis and boundary.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate of the physical position at which the Doppler reflectometer measurement is associated. It maps that measurement location to a nested magnetic surface rather than describing a cylindrical distance or a local vector component.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{m}}) = \left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{m}})-\Phi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{boundary}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{axis}}}\right]^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{m}})$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate at the measurement position, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{m}}$ is that physical measurement position, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{m}})$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the magnetic surface passing through the position, $\Phi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{boundary}}$ is its value at the last closed flux surface.

The scope is one local magnetic-surface label evaluated at the Doppler reflectometer measurement position; it is not an average, integral, or aggregate over a propagation path, channel set, or plasma region. Within the region between the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface, the value is zero at the axis and one at the boundary. It excludes the toroidal angle of the position and any signed displacement from a reference location.

This is the measurement-position specialization of the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate); the parent defines the same surface label independently of the measurement locus.

NAMES.name: poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position
NAMES.short: Geometric poloidal angle locating a measurement position around the magnetic axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) cross-section, increasing clockwise.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal angle of a measurement position is the geometric angular coordinate of a physical point about the magnetic axis in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It identifies the point's position around the magnetic axis, rather than a field-line or toroidal angle.

Taking zero on the outward radial direction from the magnetic axis, the angle is defined by

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{meas}} = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left[-\left(Z_{\mathrm{meas}}-Z_{\mathrm{axis}}\right),\,R_{\mathrm{meas}}-R_{\mathrm{axis}}\right]
$$

where $\theta_{\mathrm{meas}}$ is the poloidal angle of the measurement position, $\operatorname{atan2}$ is the two-argument arctangent that preserves the angular quadrant, $R_{\mathrm{meas}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{meas}}$ are the major-radius and vertical coordinates of the measurement position, and $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ are the corresponding coordinates of the magnetic axis.

This quantity is evaluated pointwise at the designated measurement position and is not a line average, flux-surface average, or signal-weighted aggregate. It is the measurement-position specialization of [poloidal_angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface), and it is distinct from [toroidal_angle_of_measurement_position](name:toroidal_angle_of_measurement_position), which locates the same point around the symmetry axis.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the position advances clockwise from the outward radial direction in the poloidal cross-section, viewed from the right-hand side of the symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short: Temperature-equivalent radiation energy scale of electron-cyclotron emission, evaluated at the magnetic axis, the degenerate innermost magnetic surface where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes. It is a brightness-temperature quantity, not necessarily the local kinetic electron temperature.
NAMES.long:
Temperature-equivalent radiation energy scale of electron-cyclotron emission, evaluated at the magnetic axis. The magnetic axis is the degenerate innermost magnetic surface of the equilibrium, the locus in the poloidal cross-section where the gradient of the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes; evaluation at this locus does not imply that the radiative temperature has an extremum there.

The blackbody-equivalent radiation energy scale is defined by matching the radiation field's specific intensity to the Planck spectral intensity:

$$
I_\nu = \frac{2 h \nu^3}{c^2}\left[\exp\!\left(\frac{h\nu}{T_\mathrm{rad}}\right)-1\right]^{-1}
$$

where $I_\nu$ is the radiation specific intensity, $\nu$ is the radiation frequency, $h$ is the Planck constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and $T_\mathrm{rad}$ is the [radiative temperature].

This quantity is restricted to the radiation field associated with electron-cyclotron emission at the magnetic-axis locus. For layer-resolved electron-cyclotron emission, the axis value is the radiative temperature of the resonance layer whose effective emission location is closest to the magnetic axis; the aggregation convention is nearest-layer selection, not a spatial average over neighboring layers. Ordinary-mode and extraordinary-mode electron-cyclotron emission are polarization-specific variants; the unqualified quantity does not select a polarization mode and is not a sum or mean over modes.

It is the radiation-field member of [temperature at the magnetic axis](name:temperature_at_magnetic_axis) and the magnetic-axis counterpart of [radiative temperature]. It must not be identified with the local kinetic [electron temperature at the magnetic axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) except in the limiting case of optically thick thermal emission, where the brightness temperature approaches the electron thermal energy scale.

NAMES.name: wavelength_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short: Vacuum spatial period of a probing electromagnetic wave propagating as a diagnostic beam, defining its spectral wavelength.
NAMES.long:
Vacuum wavelength of a wave beam is the spatial period of its electromagnetic phase in vacuum, assigned to the beam’s carrier radiation. It characterizes the beam itself rather than a spectral transition or an instrument-response feature.

The vacuum wavelength $\lambda_0$ is related to the beam’s temporal frequency $f$ by:

$$
\lambda_0 = \frac{c}{f}
$$

where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum and $f$ is the temporal oscillation frequency of the electromagnetic wave.

This quantity applies to a probing electromagnetic wave beam and describes its vacuum propagation property, independent of plasma-induced changes in phase velocity. It is assigned to the beam as a whole and is not a sum, average, or integral over beams, paths, channels, or spectral components. It excludes the in-medium wavelength and wavelengths associated with filters, detector pixels, or spectral transitions.

This beam-specific specialization of [vacuum electromagnetic wavelength] supplies the wavelength used to characterize the beam’s propagation and its interaction with plasma. For a vacuum plane wave, the magnitude of its [wave vector] satisfies the equivalent relation $|\mathbf{k}| = 2\pi/\lambda_0$, where $\mathbf{k}$ is the vacuum wave vector.

NAMES.name: derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_area_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Rate of change of the area enclosed by a closed magnetic flux surface’s poloidal cross-section as its signed poloidal magnetic-flux label varies.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local geometric derivative of the area enclosed by a closed magnetic flux surface’s poloidal cross-section with respect to the surface’s signed poloidal magnetic-flux label.

The defining relation is

$$
\frac{dA}{d\psi}
$$

where $A$ is the enclosed poloidal cross-sectional area and $\psi$ is the signed poloidal magnetic flux labeling the nested surface.

The derivative applies to each closed flux surface in the nested equilibrium region and is not a volume or toroidal-surface average. It describes the poloidal cross-sectional area only; it excludes the total area of the three-dimensional toroidal surface and derivatives with respect to a toroidal-flux coordinate.

This is the derivative specialization of the geometric quantity [area of a flux surface]. It is mathematically analogous to the derivative of enclosed volume with respect to poloidal magnetic flux, [derivative with respect to poloidal magnetic flux coordinate of volume of flux surface](name:derivative_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate_of_volume_of_flux_surface), with area replacing volume.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the enclosed poloidal cross-sectional area increases in the direction of increasing signed poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$; for positive plasma current, this direction is toward the magnetic axis because $\psi$ decreases outward.

NAMES.name: derivative_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_area_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Rate of change of the poloidal cross-sectional area enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface as the dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate varies.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the radial rate of change of the poloidal cross-sectional area enclosed by a closed magnetic flux surface, parameterized by the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate. It describes how neighboring flux-surface cross sections change along that coordinate.

For a nested family of flux surfaces, it is defined by

$$
\frac{dA}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}
$$

where $A(\rho_{\mathrm{tor}})$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area enclosed by the flux surface labeled by $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate.

The scope is the enclosed poloidal cross-sectional area of a closed magnetic flux surface in an equilibrium, with no averaging or summation over flux surfaces. It is a local geometric derivative along the nested-surface family, not the area of the three-dimensional toroidal surface.

This quantity is a derivative specialization of [area of a flux surface]. It is distinct from the [derivative with respect to normalized poloidal flux coordinate of area of a flux surface](name:derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_area_of_flux_surface), which uses a normalized poloidal-flux coordinate, and from the [derivative with respect to toroidal flux coordinate of volume of a flux surface](name:derivative_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_volume_of_flux_surface), which differentiates enclosed volume rather than cross-sectional area.

NAMES.name: electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Free-electron number density per physical volume, with included populations and spatial aggregation specified by applicable qualifiers or loci.
NAMES.long:
Free-electron number density is the amount of unbound electron population occupying a local physical volume. It is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the electron distribution.

For a kinetic description, the defining relation is:

$$
n_e(\mathbf{r},t)=\int f_e(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_e$ is the free-electron number density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $t$ is time, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the differential volume element in velocity space.

The unqualified quantity denotes a local physical-volume density without selecting a thermal, fast, suprathermal, or complete-population component. Its aggregation convention is local rather than line-averaged or volume-averaged; population-qualified and spatially aggregated forms are narrower instances of this general electron-density concept.

Bound electrons and ion populations are excluded. The quantity is distinct from [thermal electron density](name:thermal_electron_density), which excludes fast and suprathermal electrons, and from [total electron density](name:total_electron_density), which explicitly combines the specified electron populations.

The [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) is the path integral of local electron density divided by the complete chord length, while [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) is the corresponding average over the plasma volume. Electron density also provides the denominator in the [ratio of total ion density to electron density](name:ratio_of_total_ion_density_to_electron_density).

NAMES.name: elongation_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Ratio of the vertical to horizontal semi-axes of a nested magnetic flux surface’s poloidal cross-section, independent of its overall size.
NAMES.long:
Elongation is the shape ratio of an individual nested magnetic flux surface, describing how extended its poloidal cross-section is vertically relative to horizontally.

For a given flux surface, the elongation is defined by

$$
\kappa = \frac{a_v}{a_h}
$$

where $\kappa$ is the elongation, $a_v$ is the vertical semi-axis of the poloidal cross-section, and $a_h$ is its horizontal semi-axis.

The quantity applies separately to each nested magnetic flux surface and is a shape ratio rather than an integrated, summed, or averaged quantity. It is not restricted to the outermost surface; the distinct [elongation of the plasma boundary](name:elongation_of_plasma_boundary) refers specifically to the last closed plasma boundary.

The [radial derivative of elongation of a flux surface] describes the change of $\kappa$ across nested surfaces, whereas this quantity gives the elongation at one surface.

NAMES.name: elongation_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of the plasma boundary’s vertical half-height to its minor radius, quantifying the elongation of its cross-sectional shape.
NAMES.long:
Plasma-boundary elongation is the ratio of the vertical half-height to the minor radius of the outermost closed plasma cross-section, describing its vertical shaping relative to a circular cross-section.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the elongation is defined by

$$
\kappa = \frac{Z_{\max}-Z_{\min}}{2a}
$$

where $\kappa$ is the plasma-boundary elongation, $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the maximum and minimum vertical coordinates of the boundary, and $a$ is the minor radius, defined as the radial half-width of the boundary cross-section.

This quantity applies specifically to the plasma boundary rather than to an arbitrary nested magnetic flux surface. Its geometric aggregation uses the full vertical extent and radial half-width of the boundary cross-section; it is not a local field value and is not averaged over the boundary. It therefore excludes the corresponding elongation of an interior flux surface.

The quantity is the boundary-locus specialization of [elongation of a flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface), which applies the same geometric ratio to a general nested magnetic flux-surface cross-section.
