NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short: Dimensionless magnetic-surface coordinate locating the internal transport barrier between the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier is the dimensionless magnetic-surface label assigned to the flux surface containing the barrier. It locates that surface within the nested closed-flux region rather than giving a cylindrical distance or vector component.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ITB}) = \left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{ITB}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,LCFS}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right]^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ITB})$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{ITB})$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the flux surface containing the barrier, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,LCFS}}$ is its value at the last closed flux surface. The nonnegative square-root branch is used.

The value applies specifically to the flux surface assigned to the internal transport barrier and is bounded from zero at the magnetic axis to unity at the last closed flux surface for nested surfaces with monotonic toroidal flux. It has no species, charge-state, or spatial averaging; it is a scalar surface label.

This quantity is the internal-transport-barrier specialization of the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike the [toroidal flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier), it uses axis-to-last-closed-flux-surface normalization and is therefore dimensionless.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Dimensionless toroidal-flux label locating the top of the H-mode edge pedestal on a nested magnetic surface relative to the magnetic axis and last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The normalized toroidal flux coordinate evaluated at the pedestal top is the dimensionless magnetic-surface label assigned to the top of the H-mode edge pedestal. It locates that position within the nested closed-flux-surface family, rather than representing a cylindrical distance or a local vector component.

For a nested equilibrium, the coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ped}) = \left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{ped}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{axis})}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{LCFS}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{axis})}\right]^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ped})$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the pedestal top, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by a magnetic surface, $\mathrm{ped}$ denotes the pedestal-top position, $\mathrm{axis}$ denotes the magnetic axis, and $\mathrm{LCFS}$ denotes the last closed flux surface.

The value applies specifically at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, the inner shoulder of the edge transport barrier. Its position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). This is a single coordinate evaluation: no species, charge-state, or population aggregation applies, and no surface averaging is implied. It is distinct from a cylindrical radial distance and from the unnormalized [toroidal flux coordinate at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top).

This entry is the pedestal-top specialization of the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), with the same axis-to-boundary normalization. It should not be interpreted as the corresponding [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate), which labels surfaces using poloidal rather than toroidal magnetic flux.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Dimensionless toroidal-flux surface label evaluated on the last closed magnetic surface, serving as the outer reference for the normalized flux coordinate.
NAMES.long:
The normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma boundary is the magnetic-surface label assigned to the last closed flux surface, also called the separatrix. It identifies the outer boundary of the nested closed-flux-surface region and is not a cylindrical distance or local vector component.

The boundary value is defined by

$$
\left.\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\right|_{\mathrm{plasma\ boundary}} = 1
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate and the plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface.

This quantity is evaluated at the boundary itself, rather than averaged over the boundary or assigned to an arbitrary spatial point. It is the boundary specialization of the parent [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), whose value increases outward from the magnetic axis; the corresponding unnormalized quantity is the [toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.leaf_definition: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Number density of oxygen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all charged oxygen ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of oxygen ions at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the oxygen-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local charge-state-summed oxygen ion density at a boundary point is the zeroth velocity moment of the oxygen-ion distribution functions:

$$
n_{\mathrm{O}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z=1}^{8}\int f_{\mathrm{O}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $z$ is the positive oxygen ionization state, $f_{\mathrm{O}^{z+}}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to oxygen ions and sums the populations from singly ionized through fully stripped oxygen. It excludes neutral oxygen and other ion species, and it is a local boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the oxygen-specific instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The [flux-surface-averaged oxygen density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary) represents the same charge-state-summed oxygen-ion content averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface rather than evaluated locally.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: toroidal_beta
NAMES.short: Toroidal beta is a dimensionless measure of total plasma pressure relative to the magnetic-pressure scale associated with a toroidal magnetic-field reference, with the pressure aggregate taken as the confined-volume average of total perpendicular pressure.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal beta is a dimensionless equilibrium measure of the total pressure content of the confined plasma relative to the magnetic-pressure scale associated with a toroidal magnetic-field reference. It characterizes pressure relative to the toroidal field, with the pressure aggregate taken as the confined-volume average of total perpendicular plasma pressure.

The toroidal specialization relation is

$$
\beta_{\mathrm{tor}} = \frac{2\mu_0\,\langle p_{\perp,\mathrm{plasma}}\rangle_V}{B_{\mathrm{tor,ref}}^2}
$$

where $\beta_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is toroidal beta, $\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability, $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes averaging over the confined plasma volume $V$, $p_{\perp,\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the total plasma pressure perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction, and $B_{\mathrm{tor,ref}}$ is the reference magnitude of the toroidal magnetic field associated with the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The scope is the confined plasma in an equilibrium state. Its aggregation convention is fixed for this name: total perpendicular plasma pressure is summed over the plasma populations included in the equilibrium pressure and averaged over the confined plasma volume. This excludes local beta values, species-resolved beta values, beta definitions based on poloidal or total magnetic-field pressure scales, and beta definitions with an additional normalization.

Toroidal beta specializes [plasma beta](name:plasma_beta) by choosing the confined-volume averaged total perpendicular plasma pressure and a toroidal magnetic-field reference, with no additional normalization beyond the pressure-to-magnetic-pressure ratio. [Normalized toroidal plasma beta](name:normalized_toroidal_plasma_beta) uses the same toroidal-field beta basis and applies an additional normalization, whereas [poloidal beta](name:poloidal_beta) instead uses a poloidal magnetic-pressure scale generated by the plasma current.

NAMES.name: area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Geometric cross-sectional area enclosed by one winding turn of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil, defining its per-turn magnetic-flux coupling.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the geometric cross-sectional area enclosed by one winding turn of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil. It represents the magnetic-flux coupling area of an individual pickup-coil turn and is nonnegative.

For a winding composed of identical turns, the ideal effective flux-sensing area is

$$
A_{\mathrm{eff}} = N A_{\mathrm{turn}}
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the signed effective geometric flux-sensing area of the complete winding, $N$ is the signed number of winding turns, and $A_{\mathrm{turn}}$ is the area of one turn.

This quantity is defined per turn and applies only to the probe-coil geometry; it does not include the number of turns, winding orientation, or calibration factors. Consequently, it is distinct from the complete effective area of a flux-loop sensor, such as [area of a flux loop](name:area_of_flux_loop). The corresponding [turn count of a poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) combines with this area to determine the winding's ideal effective flux-sensing area.

sources.leaf_definition: Area of each turn of the sensor; becomes effective area when multiplied by the turns
sources.parent_definition: Poloidal field probes

NAMES.name: area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Geometric area enclosed by one complete winding turn of a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil, setting its single-turn magnetic-flux sensitivity.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the geometric area enclosed by one complete winding turn of a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil. It characterizes the coil’s single-turn coupling to magnetic flux and is independent of the number of winding turns.

For a coil with multiple turns, the effective flux-coupling area is related to the single-turn area by

$$
A_{\mathrm{eff}} = N A_{\mathrm{turn}}
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective flux-coupling area of the complete winding, $N$ is the signed [turn count of the toroidal magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), and $A_{\mathrm{turn}}$ is the area enclosed by one turn represented by this quantity.

The scope is limited to the physical area of one turn of the toroidal magnetic-field probe coil; no summation over turns, orientation sign, or additional calibration factor is included. It is distinct from the corresponding [area of a poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) and from the probe’s induced [voltage](name:voltage_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), which results from time-varying linked magnetic flux. Together with the winding count, this area determines the probe’s magnetic-flux sensitivity.

sources.leaf_definition: Area of each turn of the sensor; becomes effective area when multiplied by the turns
sources.parent_definition: Toroidal field probes

NAMES.name: length_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Physical extent of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil measured along its assigned local normal sensing axis, contributing to the coil’s magnetic-flux response.
NAMES.long:
The length of a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the physical extent of its sensing coil along the coil’s assigned local normal sensing axis. It describes the coil geometry rather than the length of a signal lead or the distance between mounting points.

This quantity applies to one poloidal magnetic-field probe coil as a whole. It is distinct from the [area of the poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), which describes the area enclosed by one winding turn, and from the [turn count of the poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), which describes the number and orientation of complete turns.

The coil length, its enclosed per-turn area, and its winding-turn count jointly characterize the probe’s magnetic-flux coupling and effective sensing geometry. The length does not itself specify the coil area, winding count, or magnetic-field orientation.

sources.leaf_definition: Length of the sensor along it's normal vector (n)
sources.parent_definition: Poloidal field probes

NAMES.name: length_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Physical length of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the non-negative axial extent of the probe coil along its local normal sensing axis. It characterizes sensor geometry and effective sensing volume; magnetic-flux sensitivity is associated with enclosed coil area and winding turn count rather than this length alone.
NAMES.long:
Physical length of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the non-negative axial extent of the probe coil along its local normal sensing axis. The probe coil is oriented so that its normal senses the toroidal magnetic-field component $B_\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the length refers to sensor geometry, not to an extent of the magnetic field.

Using projection onto the local sensing axis, the length is the span of the active winding region along that axis:

$$
L_\phi = \max_{\mathbf{r} \in \mathcal{C}} (\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}) - \min_{\mathbf{r} \in \mathcal{C}} (\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})
$$

where $L_\phi$ is the physical length of the toroidal magnetic-field probe, $\mathcal{C}$ is the active winding region of the probe coil, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of a point in that region, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the normalized local normal sensing-axis direction.

This quantity applies to one physical toroidal magnetic-field probe coil; it is not summed, averaged, or otherwise aggregated over a set of probes. As a scalar span, it is non-negative and is not a signed displacement along $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$. It excludes the probe's [enclosed area](name:area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), winding turn count, body diameter, lead length, installation position, and any path length around the device.

The product of this length with the [enclosed area](name:area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe) characterizes the probe's effective sensing volume. Magnetic-flux sensitivity of the pickup coil is associated with enclosed area and winding turn count, while the [probe voltage](name:voltage_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe) is the response quantity produced by changing magnetic flux; the corresponding [poloidal-probe length](name:length_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) uses the same projected-span convention for its probe orientation.

sources.leaf_definition: Length of the sensor along it's normal vector (n)
sources.parent_definition: Toroidal field probes

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Signed azimuthal orientation angle of a poloidal magnetic-field probe’s sensitive-axis normal in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed toroidal orientation of the sensitive-axis normal of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil. It measures the normal’s departure from the poloidal plane through the orientation of its horizontal projection.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the angle is defined by

$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{tor}} = \operatorname{atan2}(n_\phi,n_R), \qquad n_R=\mathbf{n}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}, \quad n_\phi=\mathbf{n}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\alpha_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal orientation angle, $\mathbf{n}$ is the probe’s sensitive-axis unit normal, $n_R$ and $n_\phi$ are its cylindrical radial and toroidal components, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ are the radial and toroidal unit vectors. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the signed angle from the positive radial direction to the horizontal projection of $\mathbf{n}$.

The quantity applies to the geometric orientation of each poloidal magnetic-field probe coil. It is not the local plasma magnetic field, a field component, or an angle averaged over probes, turns, or field samples. The angle determines how the probe’s sensitive direction is related to the local magnetic-field vector and therefore how the measured component is projected. The corresponding toroidal orientation for a toroidal probe is defined by [toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), while its independent poloidal tilt is represented by [poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe).
NAMES.sign: Positive when rotation from the positive radial direction toward the horizontal projection of the sensitive-axis normal is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Angle of the projection of the sensor normal vector (n) in the horizontal plane with the increasing R direction (i.e. grad(R)) (angle is counter-clockwise from above). Values should be taken modulo pi with values within (-pi/2,pi/2]. Zero if projected sensor normal is parallel to grad(R), pi/2 if it is parallel to grad(phi).
sources.parent_definition: Poloidal field probes

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: The toroidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the signed azimuthal orientation of the probe sensitive-axis normal projected onto the horizontal plane, measured from +R toward increasing φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. Opposite projected normals are folded into the same principal orientation.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the signed azimuthal orientation of the probe sensitive-axis normal after projection onto the horizontal plane spanned by $\hat R$ and $\hat\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Its zero direction is the outward radial direction, and the projected normal is treated as an orientation axis rather than a directed vector.

The angle is defined by the two-argument arctangent of the horizontal normal components, folded modulo $\pi$ into the principal interval $(-\pi/2, \pi/2]$:

$$
\alpha_\phi = \mathcal{F}_{(-\pi/2,\pi/2]}\!\left(\operatorname{atan2}(n_\phi,n_R)\right)
$$

where $\alpha_\phi$ is this toroidal angle, $n_R$ and $n_\phi$ are the radial and toroidal scalar components of the normalized probe sensitive-axis normal vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\mathcal{F}_{(-\pi/2,\pi/2]}(\beta)$ denotes the representative of an angle $\beta$ after adding an integer multiple of $\pi$ that lies in $(-\pi/2, \pi/2]$.

This quantity applies only to toroidal magnetic-field probes and is defined separately for each probe. It describes sensor orientation, not the [toroidal angle](name:toroidal_angle) that locates a point and not the probe position; no aggregation over multiple probes is implied.

With the modulo-$\pi$ folding, projections parallel or antiparallel to $+\hat R$ have $\alpha_\phi=0$, and projections parallel or antiparallel to $+\hat\phi$ have the principal value $\alpha_\phi=\pi/2$. Together with the [poloidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe](name:poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), it specifies the orientation of the same sensitive-axis normal; it is the toroidal-field-probe-specific counterpart of the [toroidal angle of a magnetic-field probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the horizontal orientation is tilted from the radial basis line toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Angle of the projection of the sensor normal vector (n) in the horizontal plane with the increasing R direction (i.e. grad(R)) (angle is counter-clockwise from above). Values should be taken modulo pi with values within (-pi/2,pi/2]. Zero if projected sensor normal is parallel to grad(R), pi/2 if it is parallel to grad(phi).
sources.parent_definition: Toroidal field probes

NAMES.name: turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Signed count of complete winding turns in a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil, fixing the orientation and magnitude of its magnetic-flux linkage.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed number of complete winding turns in a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil. Its magnitude counts the turns, while its sign records the winding orientation used to define magnetic-flux linkage.

For turns with a common flux orientation, the total flux linkage is

$$
\Lambda = N\Phi_1
$$

where $\Lambda$ is the total magnetic flux linkage of the coil, $N$ is the signed winding-turn count, and $\Phi_1$ is the magnetic flux through one turn using the probe's reference orientation.

This quantity applies to one physical poloidal magnetic-field probe coil and aggregates all of its complete winding turns, assigning one signed contribution to each turn. It is a literal coil-turn count, not the local poloidal magnetic-field value and not the geometric area enclosed by a turn.

For this probe, the literal winding count provides the physical specialization of the equivalent coupling count represented by [effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop); unlike that broader quantity, it is not a homogenized or equivalent passive-loop count that may be fractional. Together with the [area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), it determines the probe's per-turn magnetic-flux coupling. The corresponding toroidal-coil quantity is [turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe).

sources.leaf_definition: Turns in the coil, including sign
sources.parent_definition: Poloidal field probes

NAMES.name: turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Signed number of complete winding turns in a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil, with orientation referenced to the positive toroidal direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed number of complete winding turns in a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil. It represents the coil's oriented electromagnetic coupling to the toroidal magnetic-field component, rather than a magnetic-field value.

The scope is one toroidal magnetic-field probe coil. The count refers to its physical complete windings, includes their common orientation, and does not aggregate turns over multiple probes or channels. It excludes the coil's enclosed area, length, induced voltage, and any calibration factor.

Reversing the winding orientation reverses the sign. Together with the [area of the toroidal magnetic-field probe](name:area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), this count sets the ideal flux-linkage sensitivity to the toroidal magnetic field. It is the literal winding-count specialization related to the [effective turn count of a passive loop](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop), which can represent equivalent or homogenized windings and may therefore differ from a complete-turn count. The corresponding poloidal-orientation quantity is the [turn count of a poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).

The orientation is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

sources.leaf_definition: Turns in the coil, including sign
sources.parent_definition: Toroidal field probes

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_flux_loop
NAMES.short: Vertical Z coordinate of a position point associated with one flux loop in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the vertical coordinate $Z$ of a position point associated with one flux loop. It locates that point along the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Here $Z$ denotes vertical height, $R$ denotes major radius from the symmetry axis, and $\phi$ denotes toroidal angle. The value applies to an individual position point of a single flux loop; it is not a loop-area quantity, magnetic flux, voltage, or an aggregate over turns, points, or multiple loops. No population or plasma-region restriction is implied.

Together with the corresponding radial and toroidal position coordinates, this coordinate locates the flux-loop point in space. It is the flux-loop-specific counterpart of the [vertical coordinate of a measurement position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_measurement_position), which applies the same geometric concept to a generic measurement location.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the flux-loop position lies in the +Z direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: List of (R,Z,phi) points defining the position of the loop (see data structure documentation FLUXLOOPposition.pdf). Leave empty if ../type/index = 6 (differential loop)

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Vertical position of the geometric center of a poloidal magnetic-field probe, expressed as its signed Z coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical position of the geometric center of a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the signed height coordinate of the probe center in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It locates the probe center along the vertical direction and does not define the orientation of the probe's sensitive axis or the magnetic-field component measured by the probe.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical coordinate, the probe-center coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{probe}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{probe}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is the vertical coordinate of the poloidal magnetic-field probe center, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is the position vector of that geometric center relative to the coordinate origin, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector.

This quantity applies to the geometric center of a poloidal magnetic-field probe as a physical object. For a probe with finite extent, it refers to the center position rather than to the probe size, winding distribution, support structure, or any spatial average of the measured magnetic field.

Together with the [radial coordinate of a poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), it specifies the probe-center position in the $(R,Z)$ poloidal cross-section at a given toroidal angle. The same signed-coordinate concept is used for other magnetic diagnostic objects, such as the [vertical coordinate of a toroidal magnetic-field probe](name:vertical_coordinate_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), the [vertical coordinate of a flux loop](name:vertical_coordinate_of_flux_loop), and the [vertical coordinate of a Rogowski coil](name:vertical_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil), but those names apply to different objects.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the probe-center position lies above the machine midplane in the $+Z$ direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: R, Z, Phi position of the coil centre

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Vertical position of the geometric center of a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil, expressed as the signed Z coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate identifies the geometric center of an individual toroidal magnetic-field probe coil in the right-handed cylindrical basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, with coordinates $(R,\phi,Z)$. It locates the coil and does not represent the magnetic field sensed by the probe.

The coordinate is the projection of the center position onto the vertical basis direction:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{probe}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{center}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is the probe-center vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{center}}$ is the position vector from the cylindrical-frame origin to the geometric center of the coil, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector. Here $R$ denotes major radius, $\phi$ denotes toroidal angle, and $Z$ denotes vertical coordinate.

The quantity applies to one toroidal magnetic-field probe coil center. It is not summed, averaged, or weighted over windings, probes, or a spatial region. It excludes the probe's sensitive-axis orientation and the local magnetic-field value, and is distinct from the corresponding position coordinate for a [poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:vertical_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).

As the $Z$ component of the coil-center position, this coordinate complements the radial and toroidal position coordinates in locating the probe within the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the probe-coil center lies in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: R, Z, Phi position of the coil centre

NAMES.name: voltage_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Terminal voltage at a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the inductive voltage at the coil terminals caused by time variation of the local poloidal magnetic-field component in the R-Z plane of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame threading the probe windings.
NAMES.long:
Terminal voltage at a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the signed coil-terminal electromotive force associated with the probe winding that senses the local poloidal magnetic field. The sensed field component lies in the $R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and is projected along the probe sensitive-axis normal.

For a probe with algebraic turn count $N$ and geometric per-turn area $A$, Faraday's law relates the terminal voltage to the local poloidal field component $B_p$ as:

$$
V = -N A \frac{dB_p}{dt}
$$

where $V$ is the terminal voltage at the coil terminals, $B_p$ is the local poloidal magnetic-field component along the positive sensitive-axis normal, $N$ is the algebraic turn count including winding direction, $A$ is the [area of poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to one poloidal-field probe coil and is not aggregated over multiple probes. Its locus is specified by the [major radius of poloidal magnetic-field probe], [toroidal angle of poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), and [poloidal angle of poloidal magnetic-field probe]; these position quantities identify where the local field component is sampled and are not themselves voltages.

This quantity is distinct from the derived local poloidal magnetic field. It is the poloidal-field-probe counterpart of [voltage of toroidal magnetic-field probe](name:voltage_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), for a coil oriented to sense the toroidal field, and is distinct from [voltage of flux loop](name:voltage_of_flux_loop), which corresponds to a loop enclosing magnetic flux rather than a local magnetic-field probe winding.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the poloidal magnetic flux threading the coil in the direction of the probe's positive sensitive-axis normal is decreasing with time.

sources.leaf_definition: Voltage on the coil terminals
sources.parent_definition: Poloidal field probes

NAMES.name: breakdown_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Breakdown magnetic-field strength associated with local magnetic induction during plasma initiation, without selecting a particular source contribution or field-strength representation.
NAMES.long:
The breakdown magnetic field is the local field-strength characterization of the [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) relevant to plasma initiation and electron-avalanche breakdown. It represents the magnetic environment at the evaluation location without selecting a particular external-coil residual, cylindrical component, or magnitude operation.

The quantity is interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is local to the plasma-initiation setting and carries no implied species, charge-state, spatial integration, or averaging over a region.

This parent is broader than any source-specific or reduction-specific field-strength quantity. It is distinct from the [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), which is a directional cylindrical projection, and from the full magnetic-induction vector represented by [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field).

The [stray breakdown magnetic field](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field) specializes this quantity to the residual field at the plasma position produced by incomplete cancelation of external-coil fields, which can inhibit electron-avalanche breakdown. The related [stray breakdown magnetic field magnitude](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field_magnitude) further specifies a magnitude representation of that residual field.

sources.leaf_definition: Stray magnetic field at plasma position
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities

NAMES.name: poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Signed poloidal tilt angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe’s sensitive-axis normal in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured clockwise from +R.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed orientation angle of the normal defining a toroidal magnetic-field probe’s sensitive axis. It specifies the probe’s tilt in the poloidal cross-section, rather than the spatial angle of the probe center.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, let $n_R$ and $n_Z$ denote the components of the probe’s oriented sensitive-axis normal along the increasing-$R$ and increasing-$Z$ directions. The poloidal angle $\theta_{\rm pol}$ is defined by:

$$
\theta_{\rm pol} = \operatorname{atan2}(-n_Z,n_R)
$$

where $\operatorname{atan2}$ is the two-argument arctangent that preserves the quadrant of the projected normal.

The scope is one toroidal magnetic-field probe and its oriented sensitive-axis normal. This is a geometric sensor-orientation quantity, not the poloidal coordinate of the probe center, the direction of the measured magnetic field, or a plasma flux-surface coordinate; it has no plasma-population or region aggregation and is not summed over probes or coil windings.

It is a probe-specific application of the parent [poloidal angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface): the parent defines the geometric angular measure, while this quantity applies it to the probe’s oriented normal. The complementary [toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe) describes the toroidal orientation of the same probe normal, whereas [poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position](name:poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position) describes the angular location of a measurement point.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the sensitive-axis normal points from the outward radial direction toward decreasing $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, following the clockwise direction in the poloidal plane.

Zero if sensor normal vector fully in the horizontal plane and oriented towards increasing major radius. Values in [0 , 2Pi]

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_flux_loop
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of each geometric point defining a flux-loop position, measured as perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the non-negative major-radius coordinate $R$ of each geometric point defining a flux-loop position. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is the distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For horizontal Cartesian coordinates $X$ and $Y$ in a right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis whose vertical direction coincides with cylindrical $\hat{Z}$, the coordinate is defined by:

$$
R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}
$$

where $X$ and $Y$ are the point's Cartesian coordinates along $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$, and $R$ is its major-radius coordinate.

The quantity applies separately to every geometric point defining one flux-loop position, including a partial loop; it is not a loop-wide average, centroid, or other aggregation of those points. It is a geometric coordinate only and does not represent the loop's other position coordinates, linked magnetic flux, induced voltage, or [effective flux-loop area](name:area_of_flux_loop).

This quantity is the flux-loop-specific specialization of the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate): it retains the same major-radius definition while identifying the point as part of flux-loop geometry. The complete point position requires its corresponding toroidal and vertical coordinates.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate locating the center of a poloidal magnetic-field probe in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the major-radius location of the probe center relative to the toroidal symmetry axis, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, c6, Z)$ frame.

The coordinate is defined by the magnitude of the displacement perpendicular to the toroidal symmetry axis:

$$
R = \left|\mathbf{r}_{\perp}\right|
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate and $\mathbf{r}_{\perp}$ is the displacement from the toroidal symmetry axis within the plane perpendicular to that axis.

This quantity applies specifically to the geometric center of one poloidal magnetic-field probe and is not an aggregate over multiple probes or a coordinate of the measured magnetic field. It identifies the radial location only; the corresponding vertical location is given by the [vertical coordinate of the poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:vertical_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).

It is the probe-specific specialization of the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), obtained by evaluating that coordinate at the probe center.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil
NAMES.short: Radial coordinate of a Rogowski coil position, equal to the major-radius coordinate of the coil's designated geometric point in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of a Rogowski coil position is the major-radius coordinate of the designated geometric point representing the coil position. It is the non-negative perpendicular distance of that point from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Using any point on the toroidal symmetry axis as reference, the coordinate is defined by the transverse projection of the coil-position vector relative to that axis:

$$
R_{\mathrm{coil}} = \left\| (\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{coil}} - \mathbf{o}_{\mathcal{A}}) - \left[(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{coil}} - \mathbf{o}_{\mathcal{A}}) \cdot \hat{Z}\right]\hat{Z} \right\|
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{coil}}$ is the radial coordinate of the Rogowski coil position, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{coil}}$ is the position vector of the designated geometric point, $\mathbf{o}_{\mathcal{A}}$ is any position vector on the toroidal symmetry axis $\mathcal{A}$, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector along that axis, and $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm.

This quantity applies to the single designated geometric point used to locate the Rogowski coil. It is not an average, integral, or other aggregation over the winding path, aperture, conductor cross-section, or physical extent of the coil.

This coordinate is the radial member of the Rogowski-coil position coordinates and is distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the Rogowski coil](name:vertical_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil) and any toroidal angular coordinate of the same point. It is also distinct from the [area of the Rogowski coil](name:area_of_rogowski_coil), the [current of the Rogowski coil](name:current_of_rogowski_coil), coil orientation, and winding geometry; those quantities do not change the definition of $R_{\mathrm{coil}}$. As a named instance of [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), it is invariant under changes of toroidal angle at fixed major radius.

NAMES.name: current_of_passive_loop
NAMES.short: Signed conventional electric current circulating in one axisymmetric passive conducting loop, induced by changing linked magnetic flux and electromagnetic coupling.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the conventional electric current circulating in a single passive conducting loop. It represents the electromagnetically induced response of the passive conductor to changing linked magnetic flux, including transients caused by changing plasma currents, active-coil currents, disruptions, and coupling to other conductors.

For a passive loop with no separately applied circuit voltage, the linear circuit response is represented by

$$
\mathcal{R} I(t) + L\frac{dI(t)}{dt} = -\frac{d\Phi_{\rm ext}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $I(t)$ is the loop current, $\mathcal{R}$ is the loop resistance, $L$ is its self-inductance, $t$ is time, and $\Phi_{\rm ext}(t)$ is the externally linked magnetic flux, including mutual coupling and excluding flux generated by the loop's own current. The negative sign expresses Lenz's law.

The quantity applies to one passive conducting loop and denotes its net circuit current, with all induced contributions aggregated into that loop current. It excludes current imposed by an external power supply and is distinct from the current carried by the plasma or by an actively driven coil. The loop-resolved current contributes to the net [current of a passive structure](name:current_of_passive_structure) when multiple passive conducting elements form one structure.

The magnetic coupling and orientation of the loop are interpreted consistently with its [effective turn count](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop), whose sign represents the element orientation relative to positive loop current.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional current circulates in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

sources.leaf_definition: Passive loop current
sources.parent_definition: Passive axisymmetric conductor description in the form of non-connected loops; any connected loops are expressed as active coil circuits with no power supply attached.

NAMES.name: effective_turn_count_of_coil_conductor_element
NAMES.short: Signed effective winding count used to weight the magnetic-field contribution of an individual poloidal-field coil conductor element.
NAMES.long:
The effective turn count is the signed winding multiplicity assigned to one poloidal-field coil conductor element for calculating its contribution to the plasma magnetic field. Its magnitude represents the effective number of turns attributed to that element, while its sign represents winding orientation.

This quantity applies to an individual conductor element and is not the total turn count of a complete coil or coil system. It is an effective electromagnetic contribution rather than a purely geometric count of visible conductor revolutions, and it excludes the separate winding counts of magnetic-field probe coils.

For a fixed element current and geometry, the element’s magnetic-field contribution scales with its effective turn count; reversing the count reverses the corresponding field contribution. The same signed-winding concept is used for a [poloidal magnetic-field probe turn count](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) and a [toroidal magnetic-field probe turn count](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), although this quantity applies specifically to a poloidal-field coil conductor element.

sources.leaf_definition: Number of effective turns in the element for calculating the magnetic field from the coil/loop. Should be positive, unless the coil has elements going in opposite directions.
sources.parent_definition: Each PF coil is comprised of a number of cross-section elements described  individually and connected serially

NAMES.name: effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop
NAMES.short: Effective turn count of a passive loop is the signed number of equivalent windings assigned to a passive conducting loop for electromagnetic coupling. It weights the passive-loop current contribution and may be fractional for equivalent or homogenized loop elements.
NAMES.long:
Effective turn count of a passive loop is the signed number of equivalent windings assigned to a passive conducting loop for electromagnetic coupling. It may be fractional when the represented conductor is an equivalent or homogenized passive-loop element rather than a literal winding.

The signed current-turn source strength represented by the passive loop is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}} = N_{\mathrm{eff}} I_{\mathrm{loop}}
$$

where $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the signed current-turn source strength of the passive loop, $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective turn count of the passive loop, and $I_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the [current of the passive loop](name:current_of_passive_loop).

This quantity applies to the represented passive loop or passive-loop element as one electromagnetic circuit contribution. It has no implicit aggregation over multiple passive loops; if several represented windings or conductor pieces are collapsed into one loop element, their net orientation and coupling are represented by the single algebraic value of $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

It is distinct from the [current of the passive loop](name:current_of_passive_loop), which is multiplied by $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$, and from the [area of the passive loop](name:area_of_passive_loop), which describes conductor cross section. It is not a turn count for magnetic probes, coil conductor elements, toroidal-field coils, or magnetic field-line winding.

sources.leaf_definition: Number of effective turns in the element for calculating the magnetic field from the coil/loop. Should be positive, unless the coil has elements going in opposite directions.

NAMES.name: height_of_poloidal_field_coil
NAMES.short: Full vertical extent of the rectangular cross-section of one active poloidal-field coil conductor, measured parallel to Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the complete vertical dimension of the rectangular cross-section of one active poloidal-field coil conductor. It describes the conductor geometry in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with the vertical direction parallel to $Z$.

The full height is the difference between the upper and lower vertical boundaries of the rectangle:

$$
h = Z_{\max} - Z_{\min}
$$

where $h$ is the full vertical height, $Z_{\max}$ is the vertical coordinate of the upper boundary, and $Z_{\min}$ is the vertical coordinate of the lower boundary.

The quantity applies to the selected poloidal-field-coil conductor and its rectangular cross-section. It is a complete geometric extent for that member, not an average, sum, or aggregate over multiple coils or conductor elements. It is distinct from the radial cross-sectional extent represented by [width of a poloidal field coil](name:width_of_poloidal_field_coil) and from the cross-sectional area represented by [area of a poloidal field coil](name:area_of_poloidal_field_coil).

For a rectangular cross-section, this height combines with the corresponding width to determine the conducting area represented by [area of a poloidal field coil](name:area_of_poloidal_field_coil); the height itself remains the vertical dimension rather than the full cross-sectional area.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section
NAMES.short: Signed vertical position of the geometric center of a rectangular conductor cross-section in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed vertical coordinate of the geometric center of one rectangular conductor cross-section. It locates the rectangle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a rectangle with upper and lower vertical boundary coordinates, the geometric-center coordinate is

$$
Z_c = \\frac{Z_{\\mathrm{top}} + Z_{\\mathrm{bottom}}}{2}
$$

where $Z_c$ is the vertical coordinate of the rectangle center, and $Z_{\\mathrm{top}}$ and $Z_{\\mathrm{bottom}}$ are the vertical coordinates of its upper and lower boundaries.

The quantity applies to a single rectangular conductor cross-section, including a rectangular representation of an axisymmetric magnetic component. It is not summed or averaged over multiple conductors, cross-sections, or the conductor's longitudinal extent, and it is distinct from the rectangle's full vertical extent or area. For coil conductor elements, its geometric-center meaning is closely related to [vertical centroid of coil conductor element]; unlike [vertical coordinate of passive structure], it is tied specifically to the center of a rectangular cross-section rather than to a generic structure reference point.

NAMES.name: width_of_poloidal_field_coil
NAMES.short: Full radial extent of the rectangular cross-section of one active poloidal-field coil conductor, measured parallel to the major-radius coordinate R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Full radial extent of the rectangular cross-section of one active poloidal-field coil conductor is the scalar side length of that rectangle parallel to the major-radius coordinate $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to a single active poloidal-field coil conductor whose cross-section is represented as rectangular. It is the full radial extent of that one conductor cross-section, with no summation, averaging, or aggregation over multiple conductors, turns, or coil elements.

It is distinct from the [height of a poloidal-field coil](name:height_of_poloidal_field_coil), which is the full vertical extent parallel to $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is also distinct from the [area of a poloidal-field coil](name:area_of_poloidal_field_coil), a cross-sectional area rather than a side length, and from any directed displacement or position coordinate.

For the same rectangular conductor cross-section, the [area of a poloidal-field coil](name:area_of_poloidal_field_coil) is the product of this width and the [height of a poloidal-field coil](name:height_of_poloidal_field_coil).

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_arc_of_circle_center
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of an iron-core segment’s annular cross-section center in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the center of the annular cross-section representing one iron-core segment. It identifies the radial placement of that annular center in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is defined separately for each segment’s annulus center; it is neither averaged nor summed over segments. It denotes the center coordinate rather than the major-radius coordinate of an arc start point, arc endpoint, or arbitrary outline point.

The [radial outline of the iron-core segment](name:radial_outline_of_iron_core_segment) gives major-radius coordinates for points on the cross-sectional boundary, whereas this quantity gives the major-radius coordinate used to locate the annular center.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_coil_conductor_element
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of the center of a coil-conductor element’s annular cross-section in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The center major-radius coordinate locates the center of a coil-conductor element’s annular cross-section relative to the toroidal symmetry axis. It identifies the element’s geometric placement rather than a field or load.

The radial coordinate is defined by

$$
R_c = \mathbf{r}_c \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $R_c$ is the major-radius coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the annulus center, and $\hat{R}$ is the outward radial unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies separately to each coil-conductor element and refers to the center of its annular cross-section. It is not the radial coordinate of a start point, the inner or outer annulus radius, or a coordinate along the conductor path. It is the element-specific form of the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) and is distinct from the reference coordinate defined for a generic [conductor cross-section](name:radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section).

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element
NAMES.short: Non-negative major-radius coordinate of the second point in a ferritic element’s axisymmetric thick-line geometry, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the major-radius coordinate of the second point in the axisymmetric thick-line geometric representation of a ferritic element. It locates that endpoint by its distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, rather than describing the element centroid or cross-sectional extent.

The major radius is related to the point's horizontal Cartesian coordinates by

$$
R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, and $X$ and $Y$ are orthogonal horizontal Cartesian coordinates measured from the toroidal symmetry axis. The result is the $R$ coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies specifically to the second point of each ferritic element represented by an axisymmetric thick-line geometry. It is a per-point coordinate and is neither averaged nor summed over the element set. It is distinct from the first point, the oblique reference point, the geometric centroid represented by [radial coordinate of ferritic element centroid](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid), and an outline coordinate represented by [radial outline of ferritic element](name:radial_outline_of_ferritic_element).

It is a point-specific specialization of [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), obtained by evaluating the parent coordinate at the second point of the ferritic element rather than at a general geometric point or reference position.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid
NAMES.short: Nonnegative major-radius location of the geometric centroid of one ferritic element in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the radial coordinate of the geometric centroid of one ferritic element, locating that centroid by its distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The centroid radial coordinate is defined by

$$
R_c = \sqrt{x_c^2+y_c^2}
$$

where $R_c$ is the radial coordinate of the ferritic-element centroid, and $x_c$ and $y_c$ are its Cartesian coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies independently to each ferritic element and is not summed or averaged over elements. It is distinct from the [radial outline coordinate of a ferritic element](name:radial_outline_of_ferritic_element), which locates contour points, and from the [vertical coordinate of a ferritic-element centroid](name:z_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid), which provides the centroid's $Z$ coordinate. It is the ferritic-element-centroid specialization of the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate).

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_field_coil
NAMES.short: Center major-radius coordinate of an annular poloidal-field coil cross-section, measured from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The center major radius is the radial coordinate of the center of an annular cross-section representing one poloidal-field coil. It specifies the coil's axisymmetric radial placement, not the radius of the annulus or the coordinate of an outline point.

The major-radius coordinate of the annulus center is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{center}} = \sqrt{X_{\mathrm{center}}^2 + Y_{\mathrm{center}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{center}}$ is the center's major-radius coordinate, and $X_{\mathrm{center}}$ and $Y_{\mathrm{center}}$ are its horizontal Cartesian coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. Equivalently, it is the $R$ coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, measured from the toroidal symmetry axis.

This quantity applies to the annular center of one poloidal-field coil and is neither a sum nor an average over coils. It is distinct from the inner and outer annulus radii and from the coordinates of points on the coil boundary described by the [radial outline of a poloidal-field coil](name:radial_outline_of_poloidal_field_coil). As a locus-specific form of [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), it provides the representative radial position of the annular coil element.

NAMES.name: vacuum_poloidal_current_function
NAMES.short: Signed major-radius-weighted toroidal magnetic field produced by external coils in an axisymmetric current-free vacuum region.
NAMES.long:
The vacuum poloidal current function is the major-radius-weighted toroidal magnetic-field component generated by external coils in an axisymmetric current-free region.

The defining relation is:

$$
F_{\mathrm{vac}}(R,Z) = R B_{\phi,\mathrm{vac}}(R,Z)
$$

where $F_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the vacuum poloidal current function, $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, and $B_{\phi,\mathrm{vac}}$ is the toroidal component of the vacuum magnetic field in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. At a specified reference major radius, the same invariant is represented as $F_{\mathrm{vac}}=R_0B_0$, where $R_0$ is the reference major radius and $B_0$ is the vacuum toroidal magnetic field there.

This quantity applies to the combined external-coil contribution in the axisymmetric current-free vacuum region. It excludes plasma-current and other non-external-current contributions, is not the total toroidal magnetic field, and is not a per-coil value or a flux-surface average.

It is the vacuum specialization of the [poloidal current function](name:poloidal_current_function), which uses the same major-radius-weighted toroidal-field relation for the relevant equilibrium field. The [toroidal vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field) is the unweighted toroidal component, while the [difference of vacuum poloidal current function and initial vacuum poloidal current function](name:difference_of_vacuum_poloidal_current_function_and_initial_vacuum_poloidal_current_function) gives its signed change from an initial reference value.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $B_{\phi,\mathrm{vac}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Vacuum field times major radius in the toroidal field magnet. Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above
sources.parent_definition: Toroidal field coils

NAMES.name: difference_of_vacuum_poloidal_current_function_and_initial_vacuum_poloidal_current_function
NAMES.short: Signed change in the combined external-coil vacuum poloidal current function relative to its initial reference value, representing variation of the toroidal field multiplied by major radius.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed difference between the present and initial values of the vacuum poloidal current function produced by external coil currents. It represents the change in the major-radius-weighted toroidal magnetic field in the axisymmetric current-free vacuum region.

Let $F_{\rm vac}$ denote the [vacuum poloidal current function](name:vacuum_poloidal_current_function). Its change relative to the initial reference state is

$$
\Delta F_{\rm vac}=F_{\rm vac}-F_{\rm vac,initial}=R B_{\phi,\rm vac}-R B_{\phi,\rm vac,initial}
$$

where $\Delta F_{\rm vac}$ is the signed change, $F_{\rm vac}$ is the present external-coil vacuum poloidal current function, $F_{\rm vac,initial}$ is its value in the initial reference state, $R$ is major radius, and $B_{\phi,\rm vac}$ is the vacuum toroidal magnetic-field component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $\phi$ is toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity uses the combined vacuum contribution from external coil currents and excludes plasma currents and induced currents in conducting structures. It is a difference from one initial reference value, not the absolute [vacuum poloidal current function](name:vacuum_poloidal_current_function); within an axisymmetric current-free region, it inherits the parent function's spatial constancy.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the present value of $R B_{\phi,\rm vac}$ exceeds its initial reference value, with $B_{\phi,\rm vac}$ positive in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Variation of (vacuum field times major radius in the toroidal field magnet) from the start of the plasma.
sources.parent_definition: Toroidal field coils

NAMES.name: alfven_time
NAMES.short: Characteristic shear-Alfvén transit time across the magnetic-axis major-radius scale, set by local ion inertia and the reference magnetic-field strength.
NAMES.long:
The Alfvén time is the characteristic shear-Alfvén propagation time across a reference major-radius scale in the confined plasma. It is a physical MHD timescale, not an event timestamp or a growth rate.

Its defining relation is

$$
\tau_A(\rho) = \frac{R_0\sqrt{m_i n_i(\rho)}}{B_0}
$$

where $\tau_A(\rho)$ is the local Alfvén time, $R_0$ is the magnetic-axis major-radius scale, $m_i$ is the mass of the reference ion population, $n_i(\rho)$ is its number density at radial coordinate $\rho$, and $B_0$ is the reference magnetic-field strength.

The quantity applies locally at each radial coordinate in the confined plasma; it is not a radial average or radial integral, and it does not represent a charge-state-resolved time unless the reference ion population is so specified. As a timescale, it is distinct from the frequency represented by [alfven_frequency](name:alfven_frequency) and from the general temporal quantity [time](name:time). It provides the characteristic time used to normalize MHD growth rates and other dynamical rates.

sources.leaf_definition: Alven time=R/vA=R0 sqrt(mi ni(rho))/B0
sources.parent_definition: MHD modes in the confined plasma

NAMES.name: effective_charge
NAMES.short: Dimensionless effective ionic charge of a plasma mixture, given by the second ionic charge moment divided by free-electron density and indicating impurity content.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ is the charge-weighted mean ionic charge of a plasma mixture, formed from the second moment of the ionic charge distribution and normalized by the free-electron density.

The defining relation is

$$
Z_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{\sum_s n_s Z_s^2}{n_e}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of ions in species and charge-state category $s$, $Z_s$ is the positive ionic charge number for that category, and $n_e$ is the free-electron number density. For a quasineutral mixture, $n_e$ equals the sum of $n_s Z_s$ over the same ion population.

This quantity applies to the complete included ion mixture, with contributions summed over all represented ion species and charge states; it is not restricted to one species, charge state, plasma region, or spatial averaging geometry. A local value and a prescribed spatially averaged value share this same charge aggregation convention.

Effective charge is distinct from the charge number of an individual ion and from the [square of an ion charge number](name:square_of_ion_charge_number), which describes a single-species charge moment rather than the mixture-level ratio. Spatially averaged instances retain the local definition: [line-averaged effective charge](name:line_averaged_effective_charge) averages this quantity along a line, whereas [volume-averaged effective charge](name:volume_averaged_effective_charge) averages it over a plasma volume.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Thermal energy of the bulk electron population expressed as an energy-equivalent temperature determined by its random kinetic-energy distribution.
NAMES.long:
Electron temperature is the energy-equivalent measure of the mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population.

For an isotropic electron population, the defining relation is:

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_e \rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature expressed as energy, and $\langle E_e \rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron.

This is an intensive quantity for the electron population, not a sum of electron energies. It may be defined locally or after a specified spatial average, including the chord average represented by [line-averaged electron temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature) and the confined-volume average represented by [volume-averaged electron temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature). It excludes ion populations and does not itself represent total electron energy or electron pressure.

Electron temperature is related to [total electron pressure](name:total_electron_pressure) through the electron velocity-space moments; pressure additionally includes the electron number-density weighting. It is distinct from [ion charge-state temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature), which characterizes ions in a specified charge state.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate
NAMES.short: Normalized poloidal flux coordinate is a radial label for nested magnetic flux surfaces based on poloidal magnetic flux. It is zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed flux surface; for a line-of-sight locus, it denotes the minimum value reached along the line.
NAMES.long:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$ is a radial label for nested magnetic flux surfaces based on the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux). It is defined to be $0$ at the magnetic axis and $1$ at the last closed flux surface, and it identifies the flux surface associated with a local point, a measurement locus, or a flux-surface function.

The coordinate is defined from the normalized poloidal-flux difference:

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}} = \sqrt{\frac{\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}}
$$

where $\psi$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) at the local point or flux surface being labeled, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at magnetic axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), and $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the value of poloidal magnetic flux at the last closed flux surface; all values refer to the same equilibrium.

The supported region is the closed-flux-surface region from the magnetic axis to the last closed flux surface, giving $0 \le \rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}} \le 1$ for loci in that region. For a local locus, the quantity is the local value; for a line-of-sight locus, the aggregation convention is the minimum value attained along the line within the supported region. The line-of-sight value is not a path average, chord integral, or endpoint value.

The square of $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$ is the normalized poloidal-flux fraction, so the square-root form preserves poloidal-flux surface ordering while giving a radius-like label. This quantity is distinct from unnormalized poloidal magnetic flux, from a geometric minor-radius coordinate, and from the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), which is based on normalized toroidal magnetic flux rather than normalized poloidal magnetic flux.

NAMES.name: total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation
NAMES.short: Aggregate rate of irreversible electrical-energy conversion into heat by resistive current flow across the applicable conducting plasma or structure.
NAMES.long:
Total ohmic-dissipation power is the rate of irreversible conversion of electrical work into heat by finite-resistivity currents. The total aggregation covers the complete applicable conducting domain rather than one selected surface, component, or region.

For a conducting domain $V$, the power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{ohm}} = \int_V \mathbf{J} \cdot \mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{res}}\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ohm}}$ is the total ohmic-dissipation power, $\mathbf{J}$ is electric-current density, $\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{res}}$ is the resistive electric field, and $V$ is the conducting volume over which dissipation is aggregated.

For the global plasma quantity, the domain is the full plasma region and the result includes the total resistive heating associated with the plasma current, not only a local contribution or the halo-region contribution. The same physical definition applies to an explicitly named conducting locus: [power at the wall](name:power_at_wall_due_to_ohmic_dissipation) restricts the domain to wall and vessel structures, while [power of the divertor](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_ohmic_dissipation) restricts it to all divertor targets. These locus-specific quantities are distinct from the global total and exclude radiated or externally launched power.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_sawtooth_inversion_radius
NAMES.short: Dimensionless magnetic-surface label locating the sawtooth inversion radius, where the electron-temperature perturbation changes sign during a crash.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the normalized toroidal magnetic-flux label of the magnetic surface passing through the sawtooth inversion radius. This radius is the location at which the electron-temperature perturbation reverses sign during a sawtooth crash.

The value is defined by the normalized toroidal flux relation

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(r_{\mathrm{inv}})=\left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(r_{\mathrm{inv}})-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right]^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(r_{\mathrm{inv}})$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the inversion radius, $r_{\mathrm{inv}}$ is the sawtooth inversion radius, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(r_{\mathrm{inv}})$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the magnetic surface at that radius, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the equilibrium boundary.

The quantity applies to the plasma magnetic surface at the sawtooth inversion radius and is a point evaluation of the parent [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), not a volume or surface average and not a population-weighted quantity. It is not the inversion radius itself, a cylindrical radial distance, or a local vector component.

It is the parent normalized toroidal flux coordinate evaluated specifically at the inversion locus. It therefore differs from the corresponding value at the [sawtooth mixing radius](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_sawtooth_mixing_radius), which identifies the magnetic surface associated with sawtooth mixing rather than the surface where the electron-temperature perturbation changes sign.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_sawtooth_mixing_radius
NAMES.short: Normalized toroidal-flux surface label evaluated at the sawtooth mixing radius, marking the outer boundary of the plasma region homogenized during a sawtooth crash.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized toroidal magnetic-flux label of the magnetic surface passing through the sawtooth mixing radius. It identifies the outer boundary of the plasma region homogenized during a sawtooth crash.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}}) = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}})$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the mixing radius, $r_{\mathrm{mix}}$ is the sawtooth mixing radius, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}})$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the mixing surface, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the equilibrium boundary.

The scope is the single magnetic surface at the sawtooth mixing radius within the plasma region affected by the crash. This is a locus-specific evaluation of the broader [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), not a coordinate assigned to every magnetic surface, a volume average, or a flux-surface average. It is distinct from the corresponding coordinate at the [sawtooth inversion radius](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_sawtooth_inversion_radius), because the mixing radius and inversion radius represent different sawtooth characteristics.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode_center
NAMES.short: Dimensionless magnetic-surface label locating the resonant flux surface at the center of a neoclassical tearing-mode magnetic island.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized toroidal-flux label of the magnetic surface passing through the center of a neoclassical tearing-mode magnetic island. It identifies the island’s resonant surface rather than describing the island’s helical phase or radial extent.

At the island center, the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux at the island center, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its value at the equilibrium boundary.

The quantity applies to the center, or resonant-surface location, of one specified neoclassical tearing-mode island and is a pointwise magnetic-surface label, not an average over the island or a sum over modes. It is not a cylindrical radial distance, a local vector component, or the unnormalized toroidal-flux radius represented by [toroidal flux coordinate at the neoclassical tearing-mode center](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode_center).

It is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate) at the neoclassical tearing-mode center. The island’s helical orientation is described separately by its [neoclassical tearing-mode phase](name:neoclassical_tearing_mode_phase).

NAMES.short: Non-normalized toroidal-flux radius locating the magnetic surface and radial position of a neoclassical tearing-mode island center.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal-flux coordinate of the magnetic surface passing through the center of a neoclassical tearing-mode island. It provides a radius-like magnetic-surface label for the island’s radial location, rather than a geometric distance.

It is a non-negative, dimensional coordinate evaluated at the neoclassical tearing-mode center. The value represents a single locus on the nested magnetic surfaces; it is neither a surface average nor a volume average.

The quantity is the locus-specific instance of the parent [toroidal flux coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the neoclassical tearing-mode center](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode_center), it retains the dimensional toroidal-flux-radius scale rather than mapping the location to a normalized interval.
