NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states. It represents nitrogen ions specifically, rather than neutral nitrogen, electrons, or other ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{N,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{N,ion}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{N,axis}}$ is the nitrogen-ion number density at the magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{N,ion}}$ is the total number of nitrogen ions summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete nitrogen-ion population at that location, uses a sum over nitrogen ionic charge states, and excludes neutral nitrogen; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of another species.

This is the nitrogen-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It follows the same charge-state-summed convention as [helium-4 density at the magnetic axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis), while differing in the ion species counted.

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states. It represents oxygen ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral oxygen, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{O,axis}} = \left.\sum_q \frac{dN_{\mathrm{O},q}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O,axis}}$ is the oxygen-ion number density at the magnetic axis, $q$ is an oxygen ionic charge state, $N_{\mathrm{O},q}$ is the number of oxygen ions in charge state $q$, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the oxygen ion population and is summed over all oxygen ionic charge states; neutral oxygen is excluded. It is a local density, not a flux-surface or volume integral.

This is the oxygen-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs from [neon density at the magnetic axis](name:neon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local, charge-state-summed convention to neon ions.

NAMES.name: safety_factor
NAMES.short: Signed field-line winding ratio on a magnetic flux surface: the number of toroidal turns completed per poloidal circuit.
NAMES.long:
The safety factor is the signed helical winding of magnetic field lines on an individual magnetic flux surface, counting toroidal turns per poloidal circuit. It is the general flux-surface quantity, without imposing a particular evaluation locus.

The defining flux-increment relation is:

$$
q = \frac{d\Phi_{\rm tor}}{d\Phi_{\rm pol}/(2\pi)}
$$

where $q$ is the safety factor, $\Phi_{\rm tor}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the flux surface, $\Phi_{\rm pol}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux encircled by the flux-surface boundary, $d$ denotes the differential change between neighboring flux surfaces, and $\pi$ is the circle constant.

The quantity applies to magnetic flux surfaces throughout the defined plasma domain, including surfaces at the magnetic axis, internal transport barriers, and plasma boundary. It is not species-, charge-state-, or population-resolved; no particle or species summation and no volume or surface average is inherent. The toroidal magnetic-field component $B_\phi$ and net plasma current $I_p$ determine its sign, while $B_\phi$ denotes the projection of the magnetic field onto the toroidal direction and $I_p$ denotes the net current carried by the plasma.

A value at a selected locus is a specialization of the general quantity, such as the [safety factor at the magnetic axis](name:safety_factor_at_magnetic_axis) or the [safety factor at the plasma boundary](name:safety_factor_at_plasma_boundary). In contrast, [minimum safety factor](name:minimum_safety_factor) is the extremal value over the relevant flux-surface domain rather than the value at a prescribed surface. Rational surfaces satisfying $q=m/n$, where $m$ and $n$ are integer poloidal and toroidal mode numbers, are resonant with magnetic perturbations having those mode numbers. The [rotational transform](name:rotational_transform) expresses the reciprocal field-line winding convention, counting poloidal turns per toroidal turn.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal magnetic field component $B_\phi$ and net plasma current $I_p$ are parallel in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate; negative when they are antiparallel.

NAMES.name: safety_factor_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short: Signed field-line winding ratio evaluated on the magnetic flux surface designated as the internal transport barrier, giving toroidal turns per poloidal circuit.
NAMES.long:
The safety factor at the internal transport barrier is the signed helical winding of magnetic field lines on the flux surface designated as the barrier. It counts toroidal turns per poloidal circuit at that specific locus.

The defining flux-increment relation is:

$$
q_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \left.\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{d\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}}\right|_{\mathrm{ITB}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the safety factor evaluated on the internal-transport-barrier flux surface, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is toroidal magnetic flux, $\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is poloidal magnetic flux, and the subscript $\mathrm{ITB}$ denotes evaluation on that designated surface.

This quantity applies only to the flux surface associated with the internal transport barrier. It is a single flux-surface value, with no averaging or aggregation over neighboring surfaces, plasma volume, or other regions implied.

It is distinct from safety-factor values evaluated at other loci, such as the [safety factor at the pedestal top](name:safety_factor_at_pedestal_top), and it does not represent a general radial profile or a value at the magnetic axis or plasma boundary.

The [safety factor](name:safety_factor) is the corresponding locus-independent flux-surface quantity; this name specializes it by fixing the evaluation surface. The [rotational transform](name:rotational_transform) uses the reciprocal field-line winding convention, counting poloidal turns per toroidal circuit.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal and poloidal flux increments have the same sign, taking $\phi$ as the toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $Z$ the vertical height, and the positive poloidal circuit defined by increasing $\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}$.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_pressure_at_post_sawtooth_crash
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Isotropic kinetic pressure produced by random motion of bulk thermal electrons, evaluated in the plasma state immediately after a sawtooth crash.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron pressure is the isotropic scalar stress contribution produced by random motion of the bulk electron population in the designated post-sawtooth-crash plasma state. It represents the thermal electron contribution rather than the pressure of the full electron population.

For an isotropic thermal population, the pressure is defined by

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{2}{3} n_{e,\mathrm{th}}\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}\rangle
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal electron pressure, $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the number density of thermal electrons, and $\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}\rangle$ is their mean random kinetic energy; the subscripts $e$ and $\mathrm{th}$ identify electrons and the thermal population, respectively.

The quantity applies only to bulk thermal electrons and is evaluated in the plasma state immediately following a sawtooth crash. It is an isotropic scalar contribution, aggregated over the included thermal electrons, and excludes fast or otherwise nonthermal electron contributions.

It is the thermal component of [total electron pressure](name:total_electron_pressure), which combines thermal and suprathermal electron contributions. A fast-particle pressure quantity such as [fast particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) represents a distinct nonthermal population and must not be included in this thermal contribution.

NAMES.name: total_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure associated with the entire electron population, combining thermal and suprathermal contributions in the isotropic electron stress.
NAMES.long:
Total electron pressure is the isotropic kinetic part of the electron pressure tensor, representing random electron momentum transport for the complete electron population.

For the combined electron distribution function, its defining relation is

$$
p_e = \frac{m_e}{3} \int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_e|^2 f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_e$ is total electron pressure, $m_e$ is electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is mean electron velocity, and $f_e(\mathbf{v})$ is the combined electron velocity distribution function normalized so its velocity integral gives the electron number density.

The aggregation includes both bulk thermal and suprathermal electrons and applies across core, edge, and scrape-off-layer plasma. It excludes anisotropic stress components and is not restricted to the thermal electron population alone.

This quantity makes the total aggregation explicit within [electron pressure](name:electron_pressure): it is the sum of the thermal contribution and the [fast electron pressure](name:fast_electron_pressure) contribution. The parent name denotes the same isotropic pressure concept without requiring the total qualifier.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the isotropic electron stress is compressive rather than tensile.

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all positive ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all positive ionic charge states. n_{W,\mathrm{axis}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} n_{W^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete positively charged tungsten-ion population at that location, summed over charge states; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor the density of neutral tungsten or one individual charge state.

This is the tungsten-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs from [xenon density at the magnetic axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local, charge-state-summed convention to xenon ions instead of tungsten ions.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all xenon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that location. It represents xenon ions specifically, rather than neutral xenon, electrons, or another ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}

This is the xenon-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It is the on-axis counterpart of [xenon density](name:xenon_density), which applies at a general plasma location, and it is distinguished from [argon density at the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts a different ion species.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local fast electron population, excluding the bulk thermal Maxwellian component.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local fast electron population is the local continuum count density of electrons not bound to atoms, molecules, or ions that belong to the nonthermal fast-electron component.

For the fast-electron distribution, the defining relation is:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local fast-electron number density, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ is the fast-electron velocity distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the volume element in velocity space.

This quantity applies only to the local nonthermal fast or suprathermal electron population. The bulk thermal Maxwellian electron component is excluded, and no aggregation along a chord or over a plasma volume is performed; the quantity is a local component density rather than a fraction of the total population.

The parent [electron density](name:electron_density) denotes the unqualified local free-electron density. The [thermal electron density](name:thermal_electron_density) describes the complementary bulk thermal component, while the [total electron density](name:total_electron_density) combines the thermal and fast components when they are resolved separately.

NAMES.name: parallel_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Signed parallel magnetic-field component of the local total induction, resolved along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction rather than a cylindrical axis.
NAMES.long:
The parallel magnetic field $B_\parallel$ is the signed component of the local total [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) resolved along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It represents directional field strength rather than the full magnetic-induction vector or its magnitude.

The parallel component is defined by

$$
B_\parallel = \mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the local total magnetic induction, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq}$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic field, and $B_\parallel$ is the resulting field-aligned component.

This quantity is defined locally using the total magnetic induction and the local equilibrium-field direction. It has no restriction to a particular plasma source, vacuum source, physical region, or species; its aggregation convention is a pointwise directional projection, not a sum or average over components, modes, populations, or spatial regions.

Unlike the [radial magnetic field](name:radial_magnetic_field), [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), and [vertical magnetic field](name:vertical_magnetic_field), it is resolved along the local equilibrium field rather than along an axis of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike the [parallel wave magnetic field](name:parallel_wave_magnetic_field), it is not restricted to an oscillatory wave perturbation. It is the field-aligned projection of the parent [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the local total magnetic induction has a component in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic-field unit vector.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_electron_density_to_greenwald_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless Greenwald fraction comparing the electron number density averaged along a plasma chord with the empirical density limit set by plasma current and effective minor radius.
NAMES.long:
The Greenwald fraction measures the proximity of a confined plasma's line-averaged electron density to its empirical Greenwald density limit.

It is defined by:

$$
f_G = \frac{\bar{n}_e}{n_G}
$$

where $f_G$ is the Greenwald fraction, $\bar{n}_e$ is the [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), and $n_G$ is the [Greenwald density](name:greenwald_density) determined from the plasma-current magnitude and effective minor radius.

The numerator represents the electron population averaged along a plasma chord; the denominator is the empirical density reference for the confined plasma. This quantity is a global normalized ratio, not a local electron density, a density limit itself, or an average over charge states or spatial regions.

The fraction is the direct normalization of line-averaged electron density by Greenwald density: values near unity indicate proximity to the empirical reference limit, while values above or below unity indicate a line-averaged density respectively above or below that reference.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_line_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless line-averaged protium fraction among hydrogenic ions, obtained by dividing the protium density by the total hydrogenic density along the same chord.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the fraction of hydrogenic ion content carried by protium along a specified chord through the plasma. It is a ratio of consistently line-averaged densities, rather than a local fraction or a volume-averaged fraction.

$$
f_{\rm H}^{\rm line} = \frac{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}}{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}}
$$

where $f_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium fraction, $\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium-ion number density, $\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding deuterium-ion number density, and $\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding tritium-ion number density. The symbols H, D, and T denote protium, deuterium, and tritium, respectively.

The quantity applies to the hydrogenic ion population along one common chord and aggregates the isotope densities through the total hydrogenic denominator. Neutral atomic hydrogen and non-hydrogenic species are excluded. The numerator is the [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator is the [total hydrogenic density](name:total_hydrogenic_density) under the same line-averaging convention.

This ratio differs from the [ratio of volume-averaged hydrogen density to volume-averaged total hydrogenic density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density), because the latter uses volume-averaged rather than chord-averaged isotope densities.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_total_ion_density_to_electron_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of total ion number density, summed over all ion species and charge states, to local electron number density including thermal and non-thermal electrons.
NAMES.long:
The ion-to-electron density ratio compares the total particle count density of ions with the local particle count density of electrons. It is a composition and quasi-neutrality indicator based on particle counts, not on charge-weighted positive and negative densities.

$$
\mathcal{R}_{i/e} = \frac{n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}{n_e}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{i/e}$ is the ion-to-electron density ratio, $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the [total ion density](name:total_ion_number_density) summed over all represented ion species and charge states, including thermal and non-thermal ions, and $n_e$ is the local electron number density including thermal and non-thermal electrons.

The quantity applies locally at a plasma point and uses total aggregation in the numerator rather than a species-specific or charge-state-resolved ion density. It is not a charge density ratio and does not weight ions by their charge; consequently, it is distinct from [effective charge](name:effective_charge), which characterizes a charge-weighted ionic mixture.

The ratio is obtained by dividing the aggregated total ion density by the electron density, so it equals unity when those two particle number densities are equal. Its departure from unity describes the difference between total ion and electron counts and must not be interpreted alone as a direct charge-neutrality residual.

NAMES.name: tendency_of_derivative_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_volume_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Time rate of change of the volume derivative with respect to the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate for a nested magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the temporal tendency of the geometric volume metric associated with a nested magnetic flux surface. It measures how the enclosed volume gained per increment of the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate changes as the surface evolves.

$$
\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\right|_{\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}
\left(\frac{\partial V(\rho_{\mathrm{tor}},t)}{\partial \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}\right)
$$

where $V(\rho_{\mathrm{tor}},t)$ is the cumulative volume enclosed by the flux surface labeled by the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, and $t$ is physical time. The outer derivative is taken at fixed $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$.

The quantity applies to one nested magnetic flux surface and uses the cumulative enclosed volume, rather than a local shell volume or an aggregation over multiple surfaces. It has no species or particle-population restriction and is not a sum, mean, or volume average over plasma populations or flux surfaces.

It is distinct from the instantaneous metric [derivative with respect to toroidal flux coordinate of volume of flux surface](name:derivative_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_volume_of_flux_surface), which is the quantity inside the time derivative. It also differs from the corresponding derivative with respect to the poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate, [derivative with respect to poloidal magnetic flux coordinate of volume of flux surface](name:derivative_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate_of_volume_of_flux_surface).

The linked toroidal-flux volume derivative supplies the instantaneous geometric metric, while this quantity supplies its partial temporal change as the nested flux-surface geometry evolves.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local thermal electron population, excluding fast and suprathermal electron contributions.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local thermal electron population is the local continuum count density of electrons not bound to atoms, molecules, or ions that belong to the bulk Maxwellian electron component.

For the thermal electron distribution, the defining relation is:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local thermal electron number density, $f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ is the thermal-electron velocity distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the volume element in velocity space.

This quantity applies only to the local bulk thermal electron population. Fast and suprathermal electrons are excluded, and the quantity is neither a chord average nor a volume average. The parent [electron density](name:electron_density) denotes the unqualified local free-electron density without this population restriction.

The complete local [total electron density](name:total_electron_density) is the sum of this thermal component and the corresponding [fast electron density](name:fast_electron_density) when those components are resolved separately.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short: Non-negative radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface coinciding with the internal transport barrier, derived from enclosed toroidal magnetic flux rather than geometric distance.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier is the non-negative, radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface on which the barrier is located. It identifies the barrier by magnetic-surface position and is not a direct geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux:

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the associated magnetic surface, $B_0$ is the positive reference toroidal magnetic field, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

The locus is the internal transport barrier, represented as a particular nested magnetic flux surface rather than the entire plasma or a finite transport-barrier region. This quantity has no species or charge-state aggregation and is not a spatial average or an integral over a region.

It is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [toroidal flux coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike the [normalized toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier), it retains the radius-like coordinate scale rather than applying boundary normalization.

NAMES.name: total_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the complete local population, combining thermal and fast electrons rather than selecting one population component.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the complete local electron population is the local continuum count density of electrons not bound to atoms, molecules, or ions, including both thermal and fast nonthermal contributions.

The complete local electron density is defined by:

$$
n_e^{\mathrm{total}} = n_e^{\mathrm{thermal}} + n_e^{\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $n_e^{\mathrm{total}}$ is the complete local free-electron number density, $n_e^{\mathrm{thermal}}$ is the density of the local thermal electron population represented by [thermal electron density](name:thermal_electron_density), and $n_e^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the density of the local fast, nonthermal electron population represented by [fast electron density](name:fast_electron_density).

This quantity applies locally to the full free-electron population and is aggregated over its thermal and fast components. It excludes electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions, and it is not restricted to either population component. It is also distinct from [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) and [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), which apply spatial averaging rather than a local evaluation.

As the complete-population form of [electron density](name:electron_density), it includes both thermal and nonthermal contributions. Integrating this local quantity over a specified plasma volume gives [volume-integrated total electron density], whereas the component names retain only one electron population.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_effective_charge
NAMES.short: Dimensionless volume-averaged effective ionic charge of a plasma mixture, formed by averaging the local second ionic charge moment normalized by free-electron density over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged effective ionic charge is the effective charge of the complete ion mixture after spatially averaging the local charge-weighted ionic charge moment over the confined plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff},V} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},V}$ is the volume-averaged effective charge, $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge), $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average applies to the complete included ion mixture at every position, with ionic contributions summed over all represented species and charge states. It covers the confined plasma volume and is not restricted to one species, one charge state, one region, or one flux surface; it is distinct from an ordinary ion charge average.

This quantity is the volume-averaged counterpart of [effective charge](name:effective_charge). It differs from [flux-surface-averaged effective charge at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary), which averages the local effective charge over a boundary surface, and from [volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge), which represents an ordinary ion charge number rather than the second charge moment normalized by free-electron density.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, giving the global mean free-electron density.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface is the global mean of the unqualified free-electron density.

For local [electron density](name:electron_density) $n_e(\mathbf{x})$, the defining relation is:

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm LCFS} = \frac{1}{V_{\rm LCFS}}\int_{V_{\rm LCFS}} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm LCFS}$ is the volume-averaged electron density, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local free-electron number density at spatial position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_{\rm LCFS}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is a differential volume element.

The average includes the complete unqualified free-electron population within the last-closed-flux-surface volume and is not restricted to thermal or fast electrons. It is a global volume mean rather than a local value and excludes plasma volume outside that boundary; unlike [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), it is not averaged along a chord.

This quantity is the volume-averaging transformation of [electron density](name:electron_density). It provides the common denominator for volume-averaged elemental abundance ratios, such as the [volume-averaged argon-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), whose numerator and denominator are averaged over the same plasma volume.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last closed flux surface, formed from the corresponding volume-averaged densities. The argon population is summed over all argon ion charge states and excludes neutral argon.
NAMES.long:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last closed flux surface is the confined-plasma composition fraction obtained by normalizing the volume-averaged argon density to the volume-averaged electron density. The argon population is the species-level ion population summed over all argon ion charge states.

The ratio is defined as the quotient of the corresponding volume-averaged densities:

$$
C_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is this argon-to-electron abundance ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged argon-ion number density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron number density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and $V$ denotes the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface.

The scope is the confined plasma population inside the last closed flux surface, with the same volume-averaging operation applied to the argon and electron densities before forming the quotient. It excludes neutral argon, is not charge-state-resolved, and is a ratio of volume averages rather than the volume average of a local argon-to-electron density ratio.

This quantity is related to [argon_density](name:argon_density) as its volume-averaged, electron-normalized elemental abundance; [argon_density](name:argon_density) denotes the argon density before normalization to the electron population.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the quotient of the volume-averaged deuterium ion number density and the volume-averaged electron number density over the same plasma volume. The deuterium numerator is charge-state-summed over positive atomic ion charge states and excludes neutral or molecular deuterium.
NAMES.long:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the electron-density-normalized abundance of deuterium ions in a specified plasma volume. It is the quotient of the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) and the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) evaluated over that same volume.

The ratio is defined by the quotient of volume averages:

$$
f_{D,V} = \frac{\langle n_D \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{D,V}$ is this abundance ratio, $n_D$ is the [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density), $n_e$ is the electron density, $\langle n_D \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and the subscript $V$ denotes averaging over the common plasma volume.

The numerator is the volume average of deuterium ion number density summed over all positive atomic ion charge states. It excludes neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium, and deuterium bound in non-ion populations. The aggregation convention is a quotient of two volume-averaged densities, not the volume average of the pointwise ratio $n_D/n_e$.

For non-negative number densities and positive $\langle n_e \rangle_V$, $f_{D,V}$ is non-negative. It is not the fraction of deuterium among all fuel nuclei and does not represent the absolute deuterium particle inventory. It differs from the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which uses the combined deuterium-tritium numerator, while this quantity uses deuterium alone.

sources.leaf_definition: Value

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species, is the electron-density-normalized abundance of that fuel species. It compares the fuel-ion population with the electron population after each density is averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local number density of the combined deuterium-tritium effective species, $n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes averaging over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the plasma volume common to numerator and denominator; the value is a ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of a pointwise density ratio. The numerator is a species-level extensive density for the effective deuterium-tritium fuel species and is summed over all charge states before averaging. It includes only that fuel species and excludes helium ash, impurity ions, and separate isotope-composition ratios such as the [tritium-to-deuterium density ratio](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density).

Equivalently, this quantity is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) normalized by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density); it is a normalized ratio, not a derivative of either density. When the combined deuterium-tritium density is resolved into deuterium and tritium contributions over the same volume and denominator, it equals the sum of the [volume-averaged deuterium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) and the [volume-averaged tritium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3 ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by the electron average.
NAMES.long:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3 ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by the electron average and represents the global helium-3 ion composition relative to electrons.

The ratio is defined by applying the volume average separately to each density over the same confined plasma volume before division:

$$
r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e} =
\frac{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e}$ is this composition ratio, $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion number density summed over all charged ionization states, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, $dV$ is the volume element, and $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, with the same symbol denoting its volume measure in the normalization factors.

The scope is a species-level, volume-averaged, confined-plasma composition ratio. The helium-3 population includes charged helium-3 ions summed over charge states and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms; the electron population is the corresponding electron population in the same confined volume. No particular time within an evolution is part of the quantity definition.

This quantity is not the confined-volume average of the local ratio $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}/n_e$; it equals that average only for special spatial distributions. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), and its denominator is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). The [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) is the analogous isotope composition ratio for helium-4.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed flux surface, comparing the charge-state-summed helium-4 ion density with the electron density after each density is volume averaged.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed flux surface is the quotient of the volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density and the volume-averaged electron number density. It is a global isotope-abundance measure for ionized helium-4 relative to electrons in the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

The ratio is defined from independent volume averages over the same enclosed plasma volume:

$$
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}, \qquad \langle n_s\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}}\int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_s(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ is this helium-4 abundance ratio, the superscript $V$ denotes formation from volume averages, $\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged helium-4 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density of species $s$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is an element of that volume. For $s={}^4\mathrm{He}$, $n_s$ is the local helium-4 ion number density summed over all ion charge states; for $s=e$, $n_s$ is the local electron number density.

The semantic scope is species-level helium-4 ion density inside the last closed flux surface. The helium-4 numerator is summed over all ion charge states before averaging, while neutral helium-4 atoms and helium isotopes other than helium-4 are excluded. Because the numerator and denominator are averaged separately, this quantity is not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}/n_e$.

For fully stripped helium-4 ions in a quasi-neutral plasma, $2 f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ represents the helium-4 ion contribution to the electron charge balance, apart from contributions of other ions and departures from full stripping. The isotope analog is [ratio of volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), and the analogous elemental abundance quantity is [ratio of volume-averaged neon density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density). It is related to [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 ion density to electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) by the shared helium-4 numerator species, while this name explicitly normalizes by the independently volume-averaged electron density.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density is the volume-averaged tritium number density, summed over all charge states, divided by the volume-averaged electron number density.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density is the volume-averaged tritium number density divided by the volume-averaged electron number density. It expresses the tritium contribution to plasma composition relative to the electron population after both densities have been averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined as:

$$
f_{T/e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_T \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{T/e}^{V}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_T \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_T$ is the local [tritium density](name:tritium_density), $n_e$ is the local [electron density](name:electron_density), and $\langle q\rangle_V$ denotes $V^{-1}\int_V q\,dV$ for scalar field $q$ over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the specified plasma volume and the particle populations contained in that volume. The tritium density is a species-level per-volume amount and is therefore summed over all tritium charge states before volume averaging. The definition contains no selection by the time of peak electron density or by any other operating condition.

This quantity is the ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_T/n_e$, and it is not normalized to the total hydrogenic-fuel density. It is the tritium-only counterpart of the [ratio of volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which uses the combined deuterium-plus-tritium numerator; it also differs from the local [ratio of tritium density to electron density].

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Thermal energy of the bulk electron population expressed as an energy-equivalent temperature, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged electron temperature is the energy-equivalent measure of the mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.

It is defined by the volume-weighted mean of the local electron temperature:

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} T_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature, $T_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron temperature at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

This is an intensive volume-weighted mean for the bulk electron population, not a sum or a volume-integrated energy. It excludes ion populations and does not itself represent the total electron thermal energy.

The quantity is the volume-averaged form of local [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature). It uses volume weighting throughout the confined plasma, unlike [line-averaged electron temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature), which averages along a specified plasma chord. It is distinct from [thermal electron energy](name:thermal_electron_energy), which represents an extensive volume-integrated energy content rather than an intensive temperature.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.short: Dimensionless electron-temperature peaking ratio comparing the magnetic-axis temperature with the volume-averaged temperature inside the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The electron-temperature peaking ratio measures central thermal concentration by comparing the electron temperature at the magnetic axis with its volume average inside the last closed flux surface.

$$
P_{T_e} = \frac{T_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}})}{\langle T_e\rangle_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}} = \frac{T_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}})}{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}^{-1} \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} T_e(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}^3\mathbf{x}}
$$

Here, $P_{T_e}$ is the electron-temperature peaking ratio, $T_e$ is the local electron temperature, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the position of the magnetic axis, $\langle T_e\rangle_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature, $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is a position within that volume, and $\mathrm{d}^3\mathbf{x}$ is the differential volume element.

The numerator is the temperature evaluated specifically at the magnetic axis, represented by [electron temperature at magnetic axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis). The denominator is a volume average over the confined plasma volume up to the last closed flux surface; it is not a local value, a point maximum, or an average over other plasma populations. The ratio applies only to the electron population and does not represent ion-temperature peaking.

This quantity is obtained by dividing the magnetic-axis electron temperature by the corresponding volume-averaged electron temperature, so it is distinct from either operand alone and quantifies the relative central peaking of the electron-temperature distribution.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate assigned to the selected flux surface, defined as the midpoint between its minimum and maximum cylindrical R values.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the representative major-radius location of the selected flux surface, rather than the radial coordinate of one particular point. It summarizes the surface’s inboard and outboard radial extent in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

It is defined as the midpoint of the minimum and maximum major-radius coordinates on the selected flux surface:

$$
R_{\rm fs} = \frac{R_{\min} + R_{\max}}{2}
$$

where $R_{\rm fs}$ is the representative radial coordinate of the flux surface, and $R_{\min}$ and $R_{\max}$ are respectively the minimum and maximum values of the cylindrical major-radius coordinate over that surface.

The definition applies to the complete selected flux surface and uses the extrema midpoint as its aggregation convention; it is not an area-weighted, volume-weighted, or flux-weighted average. It does not denote the radial coordinate of a particular point, such as the magnetic axis or a specified midplane location.

This quantity is the flux-surface specialization of the parent [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate). It differs from the [normalized minor radius of a flux surface](name:normalized_minor_radius_of_flux_surface), which characterizes minor-radius position relative to a reference length rather than the surface’s major-radius location.
